# Overview - Time

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/book

`time` is a date and time library for Rust. It is:

- **Easy and safe**.- `time`has a- [straightforward API](https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.OffsetDateTime.html)without footguns.
- **space optimal and efficient**.- `time`provides support for dates in the ±9999 year range, with nanosecond precision; ranges up to ±999,999 are supported with the- `large-dates`feature.
- `serde`ready- `serde-well-known`feature. Not in the list?- [Make your format](https://time-rs.github.io/api/format-description.html).
- `const`ready- `const`, making it ready for resource-constrained applications, with optional- [macros](https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/macros/index.html)for easy date creation.
- `no-std`support- `alloc`and- `std`features.
- **numeric traits**. Use durations easily:- `2.seconds()`.
- Supports Windows, Linux, macOS,
[WebAssembly](https://developer.mozilla.org/fr/docs/WebAssembly)targets among others.

And more…

This short tutorial describes basic usage of `time`, to get operational quickly.

- **Install**. Add it to your- `time`- `Cargo.toml`. We’ll enable- `macros`:

```
[dependencies]
time = { version = "0.3", features = ["macros"] }
```
- **Get the current time**With the crate feature- `std`a UTC offset (- `OffsetDateTime`- `local-offset`, we can also get the local time.

```
use time::OffsetDateTime;
let now = OffsetDateTime::now_utc();
// let local = OffsetDateTime::now_local();
println!("{now}");
```
- **Create dates and times.**We can create dates (- `Date`- `PrimitiveDateTime`- `OffsetDateTime`- `Time`

```
use time::{Date, PrimitiveDateTime, OffsetDateTime, UtcOffset};
use time::Weekday::Wednesday;
let date = Date::from_iso_week_date(2022, 1, Wednesday).unwrap();
let datetime = date.with_hms(13, 0, 55).unwrap();
let datetime_off = datetime.assume_offset(UtcOffset::from_hms(1, 2, 3).unwrap());
println!("{date}, {datetime}, {datetime_off}");
// 2022-01-01, 2022-01-01 13:00:55.0, 2022-01-01 13:00:55.0 +01:02:03
```
With the `macros` feature:

```
use time::macros::{date, datetime};
let date = date!(2022-01-01);
let datetime = datetime!(2022-01-01 13:00:55);
let datetime_off = datetime!(2022-01-01 13:00:55 +1:02:03);
println!("{date}, {datetime}, {datetime_off}");
// 2022-01-01, 2022-01-01 13:00:55.0, 2022-01-01 13:00:55.0 +01:02:03
```
- **Manipulate dates and use**:- `Duration`s

```
use time::Duration;
use time::macros::{datetime};
let a = datetime!(2022-01-01 10:00:55);
let b = datetime!(2022-01-01 13:00:00);
let duration: Duration = b - a;
println!("{}", b - a);
// 2h59m5s
```
time 0.1 was originally a thin wrapper around libc time functions. Because it was relatively
barebones, [ chrono](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.19/chrono/) was developed as a richer API on top
of time 0.1.

Around 2019, the time crate, which was unmaintained since August 2016, was picked up for maintenance
again. `time` has since been rewritten as of time 0.2, and is incompatible with the 0.1 version.

Today:

- `time`has been rewritten from 0.1, and is actively developed.
- `chrono`depends on time 0.1, an old version unrelated with current- `time`, and is actively developed as well.

Since they are incompatible with each other, please choose the library that fits your needs.

# time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time

## Expand description

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#feature-flags)Feature flags

This crate exposes a number of features. These can be enabled or disabled as shown
[in Cargo’s documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html). Features
are *disabled* by default unless otherwise noted.

Reliance on a given feature is always indicated alongside the item definition.

-
`std`(*enabled by default, implicitly enables*)`alloc`This enables a number of features that depend on the standard library.
-
`alloc`(*enabled by default via*)`std`Enables a number of features that require the ability to dynamically allocate memory.
-
`macros`Enables macros that provide compile-time verification of values and intuitive syntax.
-
`formatting`(*implicitly enables*)`std`Enables formatting of most structs.
-
`parsing`Enables parsing of most structs.
-
`local-offset`(*implicitly enables*)`std`This feature enables a number of methods that allow obtaining the system’s UTC offset.
-
`large-dates`By default, only years within the ±9999 range (inclusive) are supported. If you need support for years outside this range, consider enabling this feature; the supported range will be increased to ±999,999. Note that enabling this feature has some costs, as it means forgoing some optimizations. Ambiguities may be introduced when parsing that would not otherwise exist.
-
`serde`Enables `serde`
-
`serde-human-readable`(*implicitly enables*)`serde`,`formatting`, and`parsing`Allows `serde`representations to use a human-readable format. This is determined by the serializer, not the user. If this feature is not enabled or if the serializer requests a non-human-readable format, a format optimized for binary representation will be used.Libraries should never enable this feature, as the decision of what format to use should be up to the user.
-
`rand`(*implicitly enables*)`rand08`,`rand09`, and`rand010`Previously, this would enable support for `rand`0.8. Since the release of`rand`0.9, the feature has been split into`rand08`and`rand09`to allow support for both versions.`rand`0.10 has since been added. For backwards compatibility and simplicity, this feature enables support for*all*series.It is strongly recommended to enable the version you need directly, as enabling `rand`will needlessly pull in all versions.
-
`rand08`,`rand09`,`rand010`Enables `rand`0.8`rand`0.9`rand`0.10
-
`quickcheck`(*implicitly enables*)`alloc`Enables [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/quickcheck)support for all types.
-
`wasm-bindgen`Enables `wasm-bindgen`[JavaScript dates](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-bindgen/api/js_sys/struct.Date.html), as well as obtaining the UTC offset from JavaScript.

`UtcOffset````
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2000-01-01 0:00 UTC)
        .to_offset(offset!(-1))
        .year(),
    1999,
);
// Let's see what time Sydney's new year's celebration is in New York and Los Angeles.
// Construct midnight on new year's in Sydney.
let sydney = datetime!(2000-01-01 0:00 +11);
let new_york = sydney.to_offset(offset!(-5));
let los_angeles = sydney.to_offset(offset!(-8));
assert_eq!(sydney.hour(), 0);
assert_eq!(new_york.hour(), 8);
assert_eq!(los_angeles.hour(), 5);
```

This method panics if the local date-time in the new offset is outside the supported range.

Create an `OffsetDateTime` from the provided Unix timestamp. Calling `.offset()` on the
resulting value is guaranteed to return UTC.

```
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(0),
    Ok(OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH),
);
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(1_546_300_800),
    Ok(datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00 UTC)),
);
```
If you have a timestamp-nanosecond pair, you can use something along the lines of the following:

#### pub const fn [to_iso_week_date](https://time-rs.github.io#method.to_iso_week_date)(self) -> ([i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), [Weekday](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.Weekday.html))

Get the ISO 8601 year, week number, and weekday.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00 UTC).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 1, Tuesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2019-10-04 0:00 UTC).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 40, Friday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 0:00 UTC).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 1, Wednesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-12-31 0:00 UTC).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Thursday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2021-01-01 0:00 UTC).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Friday)
);
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#997-999)#### pub const fn [checked_add](https://time-rs.github.io#method.checked_add)(self, duration: [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Duration.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#997-999)

#### pub const fn [checked_add](https://time-rs.github.io#method.checked_add)(self, duration: [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Duration.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

Computes `self + duration`, returning `None` if an overflow occurred.

```
let datetime = Date::MIN.midnight().assume_offset(offset!(+10));
assert_eq!(datetime.checked_add((-2).days()), None);
let datetime = Date::MAX.midnight().assume_offset(offset!(+10));
assert_eq!(datetime.checked_add(2.days()), None);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2019-11-25 15:30 +10).checked_add(27.hours()),
    Some(datetime!(2019-11-26 18:30 +10))
);
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1157-1159)#### pub const fn [replace_time](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_time)(self, time: [Time](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Time.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1157-1159)

#### pub const fn [replace_time](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_time)(self, time: [Time](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Time.html)) -> Self

Replace the time, which is assumed to be in the stored offset. The date and offset components are unchanged.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 5:00 UTC).replace_time(time!(12:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 UTC)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 -5).replace_time(time!(7:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 7:00 -5)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 0:00 +1).replace_time(time!(12:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 +1)
);
```

Replace the year. The month and day will be unchanged.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00 +01).replace_year(2019),
    Ok(datetime!(2019-02-18 12:00 +01))
);
assert!(datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00 +01).replace_year(-1_000_000_000).is_err()); // -1_000_000_000 isn't a valid year
assert!(datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00 +01).replace_year(1_000_000_000).is_err()); // 1_000_000_000 isn't a valid year
```

`formatting`[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1568-1574)**crate feature **`parsing` only.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1568-1574)

**crate feature**only.

`parsing`Parse an `OffsetDateTime` from the input using the provided [format
description](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/index.html) and default values.

```
let format = format_description!("[year]-[month]-[day] [hour]:[minute]");
let defaults = Parsed::new()
    .with_offset_hour(0).expect("0 is a valid offset hour")
    .with_offset_minute_signed(0).expect("0 is a valid offset minute");
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::parse_with_defaults(b"2020-01-02 03:04", &format, defaults)?,
    datetime!(2020-01-02 03:04 +0:00)
);
```

# Duration in time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.Duration.html

`pub struct Duration { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A span of time with nanosecond precision.

Each `Duration` is composed of a whole number of seconds and a fractional part represented in
nanoseconds.

This implementation allows for negative durations, unlike [ core::time::Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html).

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

The minimum possible duration. Adding any negative duration to this will cause an overflow.

The maximum possible duration. Adding any positive duration to this will cause an overflow.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/duration.rs.html#385-390)#### pub const fn [unsigned_abs](https://time-rs.github.io#method.unsigned_abs)(self) -> [StdDuration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/duration.rs.html#385-390)

#### pub const fn [unsigned_abs](https://time-rs.github.io#method.unsigned_abs)(self) -> [StdDuration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)

Create a new `Duration` with the provided seconds and nanoseconds. If nanoseconds is at
least ±109, it will wrap to the number of seconds.

```
assert_eq!(Duration::new(1, 0), 1.seconds());
assert_eq!(Duration::new(-1, 0), (-1).seconds());
assert_eq!(Duration::new(1, 2_000_000_000), 3.seconds());
```
[§](https://time-rs.github.io#panics)Panics

This may panic if an overflow occurs.

#### pub const fn [saturating_seconds_f64](https://time-rs.github.io#method.saturating_seconds_f64)(seconds: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> Self

Creates a new `Duration` from the specified number of seconds
represented as `f64`. Any values that are out of bounds are saturated at
the minimum or maximum respectively. `NaN` gets turned into a `Duration`
of 0 seconds.

```
assert_eq!(Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(0.5), 0.5.seconds());
assert_eq!(Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(-0.5), (-0.5).seconds());
assert_eq!(
    Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::NAN),
    Duration::new(0, 0),
);
assert_eq!(
    Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::NEG_INFINITY),
    Duration::MIN,
);
assert_eq!(
    Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::INFINITY),
    Duration::MAX,
);
```

assert_eq!(Duration::MIN.saturating_mul(2), Duration::MIN);
assert_eq!(Duration::MAX.saturating_mul(-2), Duration::MIN);
assert_eq!(Duration::MIN.saturating_mul(-2), Duration::MAX);
```

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#impl-Display-for-Duration)

The format returned by this implementation is not stable and must not be relied upon.

By default this produces an exact, full-precision printout of the duration.
For a concise, rounded printout instead, you can use the `.N` format specifier:

For the purposes of this implementation, a day is exactly 24 hours and a minute is exactly 60 seconds.

# time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#feature-flags)Feature flags

This crate exposes a number of features. These can be enabled or disabled as shown
[in Cargo’s documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html). Features
are *disabled* by default unless otherwise noted.

Reliance on a given feature is always indicated alongside the item definition.

-
`std`(*enabled by default, implicitly enables*)`alloc`This enables a number of features that depend on the standard library.
-
`alloc`(*enabled by default via*)`std`Enables a number of features that require the ability to dynamically allocate memory.
-
`macros`Enables macros that provide compile-time verification of values and intuitive syntax.
-
`formatting`(*implicitly enables*)`std`Enables formatting of most structs.
-
`parsing`Enables parsing of most structs.
-
`local-offset`(*implicitly enables*)`std`This feature enables a number of methods that allow obtaining the system’s UTC offset.
-
`large-dates`By default, only years within the ±9999 range (inclusive) are supported. If you need support for years outside this range, consider enabling this feature; the supported range will be increased to ±999,999. Note that enabling this feature has some costs, as it means forgoing some optimizations. Ambiguities may be introduced when parsing that would not otherwise exist.
-
`serde`Enables `serde`
-
`serde-human-readable`(*implicitly enables*)`serde`,`formatting`, and`parsing`Allows `serde`representations to use a human-readable format. This is determined by the serializer, not the user. If this feature is not enabled or if the serializer requests a non-human-readable format, a format optimized for binary representation will be used.Libraries should never enable this feature, as the decision of what format to use should be up to the user.
-
`rand`(*implicitly enables*)`rand08`,`rand09`, and`rand010`Previously, this would enable support for `rand`0.8. Since the release of`rand`0.9, the feature has been split into`rand08`and`rand09`to allow support for both versions.`rand`0.10 has since been added. For backwards compatibility and simplicity, this feature enables support for*all*series.It is strongly recommended to enable the version you need directly, as enabling `rand`will needlessly pull in all versions.
-
`rand08`,`rand09`,`rand010`Enables `rand`0.8`rand`0.9`rand`0.10
-
`quickcheck`(*implicitly enables*)`alloc`Enables [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/quickcheck)support for all types.
-
`wasm-bindgen`Enables `wasm-bindgen`[JavaScript dates](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-bindgen/api/js_sys/struct.Date.html), as well as obtaining the UTC offset from JavaScript.

[287](https://time-rs.github.io#287)        doc = "    datetime!(+999999-12-31 23:59:59 -1).checked_to_utc(),"
[288](https://time-rs.github.io#288)    )]
[289](https://time-rs.github.io#289)    #[cfg_attr(
[290](https://time-rs.github.io#290)        not(feature = "large-dates"),
[291](https://time-rs.github.io#291)        doc = "    datetime!(9999-12-31 23:59:59 -1).checked_to_utc(),"

[409](https://time-rs.github.io#409)    /// Create an `OffsetDateTime` from the provided Unix timestamp. Calling `.offset()` on the
[410](https://time-rs.github.io#410)    /// resulting value is guaranteed to return UTC.
[411](https://time-rs.github.io#411)    ///
[412](https://time-rs.github.io#412)    /// ```rust
[413](https://time-rs.github.io#413)    /// # use time::OffsetDateTime;
[414](https://time-rs.github.io#414)    /// # use time_macros::datetime;
[415](https://time-rs.github.io#415)    /// assert_eq!(
[416](https://time-rs.github.io#416)    ///     OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(0),
[417](https://time-rs.github.io#417)    ///     Ok(OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH),
[418](https://time-rs.github.io#418)    /// );
[419](https://time-rs.github.io#419)    /// assert_eq!(
[420](https://time-rs.github.io#420)    ///     OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(1_546_300_800),
[421](https://time-rs.github.io#421)    ///     Ok(datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00 UTC)),
[422](https://time-rs.github.io#422)    /// );
[423](https://time-rs.github.io#423)    /// ```
[424](https://time-rs.github.io#424)    ///
[425](https://time-rs.github.io#425)    /// If you have a timestamp-nanosecond pair, you can use something along the lines of the
[426](https://time-rs.github.io#426)    /// following:
[427](https://time-rs.github.io#427)    ///
[428](https://time-rs.github.io#428)    /// ```rust
[429](https://time-rs.github.io#429)    /// # use time::{Duration, OffsetDateTime, ext::NumericalDuration};
[430](https://time-rs.github.io#430)    /// let (timestamp, nanos) = (1, 500_000_000);
[431](https://time-rs.github.io#431)    /// assert_eq!(
[432](https://time-rs.github.io#432)    ///     OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(timestamp)? + Duration::nanoseconds(nanos),
[433](https://time-rs.github.io#433)    ///     OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH + 1.5.seconds()
[434](https://time-rs.github.io#434)    /// );
[435](https://time-rs.github.io#435)    /// # Ok::<_, time::Error>(())
[436](https://time-rs.github.io#436)    /// ```
[437](https://time-rs.github.io#437)    #[inline]

[473](https://time-rs.github.io#473)    /// Construct an `OffsetDateTime` from the provided Unix timestamp (in nanoseconds). Calling
[474](https://time-rs.github.io#474)    /// `.offset()` on the resulting value is guaranteed to return UTC.
[475](https://time-rs.github.io#475)    ///
[476](https://time-rs.github.io#476)    /// ```rust
[477](https://time-rs.github.io#477)    /// # use time::OffsetDateTime;

[480](https://time-rs.github.io#480)    ///     OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp_nanos(0),

[482](https://time-rs.github.io#482)    /// );
[483](https://time-rs.github.io#483)    /// assert_eq!(
[484](https://time-rs.github.io#484)    ///     OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp_nanos(1_546_300_800_000_000_000),
[485](https://time-rs.github.io#485)    ///     Ok(datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00 UTC)),
[486](https://time-rs.github.io#486)    /// );
[487](https://time-rs.github.io#487)    /// ```
[488](https://time-rs.github.io#488)    #[inline]

[531](https://time-rs.github.io#531)        let days = ([self](https://time-rs.github.io#530).[to_julian_day](https://time-rs.github.io#802-804)() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html) - [UNIX_EPOCH_JULIAN_DAY](https://time-rs.github.io#34) as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html))
[532](https://time-rs.github.io#532)            * [Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Second.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Day](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Day.html));
[533](https://time-rs.github.io#533)        let hours = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#530).[hour](https://time-rs.github.io#887-889)() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html) * [Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Second.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Hour](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Hour.html));
[534](https://time-rs.github.io#534)        let minutes = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#530).[minute](https://time-rs.github.io#906-908)() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html) * [Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Second.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Minute](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Minute.html));
[535](https://time-rs.github.io#535)        let seconds = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#530).[second](https://time-rs.github.io#925-927)() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html);
[536](https://time-rs.github.io#536)        let offset_seconds = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#530).offset.[whole_seconds](https://time-rs.github.io/utc_offset.rs.html#376-380)() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html);
[537](https://time-rs.github.io#537)        [days](https://time-rs.github.io#531) + [hours](https://time-rs.github.io#533) + [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#534) + [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#535) - [offset_seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#536)

[929](https://time-rs.github.io#929)    // Because a `UtcOffset` is limited in resolution to one second, any subsecond value will not
[930](https://time-rs.github.io#930)    // change when adjusting for the offset.
[931](https://time-rs.github.io#931)

[1576](https://time-rs.github.io#1576)    /// A helper method to check if the `OffsetDateTime` is a valid representation of a leap second.
[1577](https://time-rs.github.io#1577)    /// Leap seconds, when parsed, are represented as the preceding nanosecond. However, leap
[1578](https://time-rs.github.io#1578)    /// seconds can only occur as the last second of a month UTC.
[1579](https://time-rs.github.io#1579)    #[cfg(feature = "parsing")]
[1580](https://time-rs.github.io#1580)    #[inline]
[1581](https://time-rs.github.io#1581)    pub(crate) const fn is_valid_leap_second_stand_in(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) {
[1582](https://time-rs.github.io#1582)        // This comparison doesn't need to be adjusted for the stored offset, so check it first for
[1583](https://time-rs.github.io#1583)        // speed.
[1584](https://time-rs.github.io#1584)        if [self](https://time-rs.github.io#1581).[nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io#976-978)() != 999_999_999 {
[1585](https://time-rs.github.io#1585)            return false;
[1586](https://time-rs.github.io#1586)        }
[1587](https://time-rs.github.io#1587)
[1588](https://time-rs.github.io#1588)        let (year, ordinal, time) = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#1581).[to_utc_raw](https://time-rs.github.io#318-358)();
[1589](https://time-rs.github.io#1589)        let [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(date) = [Date](https://time-rs.github.io/date.rs.html#50-57)::[from_ordinal_date](https://time-rs.github.io/date.rs.html#188-203)([year](https://time-rs.github.io#1588), [ordinal](https://time-rs.github.io#1588)) else {
[1590](https://time-rs.github.io#1590)            return false;
[1591](https://time-rs.github.io#1591)        };
[1592](https://time-rs.github.io#1592)
[1593](https://time-rs.github.io#1593)        [time](https://time-rs.github.io#1588).[hour](https://time-rs.github.io/time.rs.html#392-394)() == 23
[1594](https://time-rs.github.io#1594)            && [time](https://time-rs.github.io#1588).[minute](https://time-rs.github.io/time.rs.html#406-408)() == 59
[1595](https://time-rs.github.io#1595)            && [time](https://time-rs.github.io#1588).[second](https://time-rs.github.io/time.rs.html#420-422)() == 59
[1596](https://time-rs.github.io#1596)            && [date](https://time-rs.github.io#1589).[day](https://time-rs.github.io/date.rs.html#397-411)() == [date](https://time-rs.github.io#1589).[month](https://time-rs.github.io/date.rs.html#365-385)().[length](https://time-rs.github.io/month.rs.html#70-72)([year](https://time-rs.github.io#1588))
[1597](https://time-rs.github.io#1597)    }

# PrimitiveDateTime in time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html

Struct PrimitiveDateTime    Copy item path  Source  `pub struct PrimitiveDateTime {  }`Expand description The smallest value that can be represented by `PrimitiveDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

With `large-dates` disabled it is equal to `-9999-01-01 00:00:00.0`
With `large-dates` enabled it is equal to `-999999-01-01 00:00:00.0`

With `large-dates` enabled it is equal to `999999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`

# UtcOffset in time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.UtcOffset.html

`pub struct UtcOffset { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An offset from UTC.

This struct can store values up to ±25:59:59. If you need support outside this range, please file an issue with your use case.

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset by the number of hours, minutes, and seconds
provided.

The sign of all three components should match. If they do not, all smaller components will have their signs flipped.

# Date in time - Rust

`pub struct Date { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Date in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

By default, years between ±9999 inclusive are representable. This can be expanded to ±999,999
inclusive by enabling the `large-dates` crate feature. Doing so has performance implications
and introduces some ambiguities when parsing.

Get the ISO 8601 year, week number, and weekday.

```
assert_eq!(date!(2019-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2019, 1, Tuesday));

assert_eq!(date!(2020-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 1, Wednesday));
assert_eq!(date!(2020-12-31).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 53, Thursday));
assert_eq!(date!(2021-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 53, Friday));
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/date.rs.html#809-837)#### pub const fn [checked_add](https://time-rs.github.io#method.checked_add)(self, duration: [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Duration.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/date.rs.html#809-837)

#### pub const fn [checked_add](https://time-rs.github.io#method.checked_add)(self, duration: [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Duration.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

Computes `self + duration`, returning `None` if an overflow occurred.

```
assert_eq!(Date::MAX.checked_add(1.days()), None);
assert_eq!(Date::MIN.checked_add((-2).days()), None);
assert_eq!(
    date!(2020-12-31).checked_add(2.days()),
    Some(date!(2021-01-02))
);
```
[§](https://time-rs.github.io#note)Note

This function only takes whole days into account.

# Time in time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.Time.html

`pub struct Time { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The clock time within a given date. Nanosecond precision.

All minutes are assumed to have exactly 60 seconds; no attempt is made to handle leap seconds (either positive or negative).

When comparing two `Time`s, they are assumed to be in the same calendar date.

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

Attempt to create a `Time` from the hour, minute, and second.

Struct UtcDateTime   Copy item path  Source  `pub struct UtcDateTime {  }`Expand description A `PrimitiveDateTime`

`UtcDateTime` is guaranteed to be ABI-compatible with `PrimitiveDateTime`

Midnight, 1 January, 1970.

assert_eq! (UtcDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH, utc_datetime! (1970 -01 -01 0 :00 ));The smallest value that can be represented by `UtcDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

With `large-dates` disabled it is equal to `-9999-01-01 00:00:00.0`
With `large-dates` enabled it is equal to `-999999-01-01 00:00:00.0`

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

With `large-dates` disabled it is equal to `9999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`
With `large-dates` enabled it is equal to `999999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`

pub enum Weekday {
    Monday = 0,
    Tuesday = 1,
    Wednesday = 2,
    Thursday = 3,
    Friday = 4,
    Saturday = 5,
    Sunday = 6,
}Expand description Days of the week.

As order is dependent on context (Sunday could be either two days after or five days before
Friday), this type does not implement `PartialOrd` or `Ord`.

# time::format_description - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/format_description/index.html

**crate features**only.

`formatting` or `parsing`## Expand description

Description of how types should be formatted and parsed.

The formatted value will be output to the provided writer. Format descriptions can be
[well-known](https://time-rs.github.io/well_known/index.html) or obtained by using the
[ format_description!](https://time-rs.github.io/macros/macro.format_description.html) macro or a function listed below.

For examples, see the implementors of [Formattable](https://time-rs.github.io/formatting/trait.Formattable.html),
e.g. [ well_known::Rfc3339](https://time-rs.github.io/well_known/struct.Rfc3339.html).

## Modules[§](https://time-rs.github.io#modules)

- [modifier](https://time-rs.github.io/modifier/index.html)
- Various modifiers for components.
- [well_](https://time-rs.github.io/well_known/index.html)- known
- Well-known formats, typically standards.

## Structs[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structs)

- [Format](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.FormatDescriptionV3.html)- Description - V3
- A complete description of how to format and parse a type.

## Enums[§](https://time-rs.github.io#enums)

- [Borrowed](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.BorrowedFormatItem.html)- Format - Item
- A complete description of how to format and parse a type.
- [Component](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.Component.html)
- A component of a larger format description.
- [Owned](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.OwnedFormatItem.html)- Format - Item - `alloc`
- A complete description of how to format and parse a type.

## Functions[§](https://time-rs.github.io#functions)

- [parse](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse.html)- Deprecated - `alloc`
- Parse a sequence of items from the format description.
- [parse_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse_borrowed.html)- borrowed - `alloc`
- Parse a sequence of items from the format description.
- [parse_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse_owned.html)- owned - `alloc`
- Parse a sequence of items from the format description.
- [parse_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse_strftime_borrowed.html)- strftime_ - borrowed - `alloc`
- Parse a sequence of items from the `strftime`format description
- [parse_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse_strftime_owned.html)- strftime_ - owned - `alloc`
- Parse a sequence of items from the `strftime`format description

## Type Aliases[§](https://time-rs.github.io#types)

- [Static](https://time-rs.github.io/type.StaticFormatDescription.html)- Format - Description
- The type output by the `format_description!`

# Parsed in time::parsing - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/parsing/struct.Parsed.html

`pub struct Parsed { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`parsing`## Expand description

All information parsed.

This information is directly used to construct the final values.

Most users will not need think about this struct in any way. It is public to allow for manual control over values, in the instance that the default parser is insufficient.

Obtain the `iso_year_century_is_negative` component.

This indicates whether the value returned from `iso_year_century` is negative. If the year
is zero, it is necessary to call this method for disambiguation.

All setters return `Option<()>`, which is `Some` if the value was set, and `None` if not. The
setters *may* fail if the value is invalid, though behavior is not guaranteed.

If the value is zero, the sign of the century is taken from the second parameter. Otherwise the sign is inferred from the value.

# Timestamp in time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/struct.Timestamp.html

`pub struct Timestamp { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A Unix timestamp with nanosecond precision.

This type represents a point in time as a number of seconds and nanoseconds elapsed since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). Negative values represent times before the Unix epoch.

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

The minimum valid `Timestamp`.

The moment in time represented by this value may vary depending on the feature flags enabled.

The maximum valid `Timestamp`.

The moment in time represented by this value may vary depending on the feature flags enabled.

assert_eq!(
    timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(1),
    Ok(timestamp!(1_546_311_845))
);
assert!(timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(0).is_err()); // 0 isn't a valid day of the year
assert!(timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(366).is_err()); // the timestamp is in 2019, which isn't a leap year

[4](https://time-rs.github.io#4)///

[13](https://time-rs.github.io#13)///     Date::from_iso_week_date(2020, 1, Wednesday)?
[14](https://time-rs.github.io#14)/// );
[15](https://time-rs.github.io#15)/// assert_eq!(date!(2020-001), Date::from_ordinal_date(2020, 1)?);

[17](https://time-rs.github.io#17)///     date!(2020-01-01),
[18](https://time-rs.github.io#18)///     Date::from_calendar_date(2020, Month::January, 1)?

# date in time::macros - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/macros/macro.date.html

# Macro date

[Source](../../src/time_macros/lib.rs.html#56) `date!() {  }`

Available on **crate feature **`macros` only.

## Expand description

Construct a `Date`

The resulting expression can be used in `const` or `static` declarations.

Three formats are supported: year-week-weekday, year-ordinal, and year-month-day.

```
assert_eq!(
    date!(2020-W01-3),
    Date::from_iso_week_date(2020, 1, Wednesday)?
);
assert_eq!(date!(2020-001), Date::from_ordinal_date(2020, 1)?);
assert_eq!(
    date!(2020-01-01),
    Date::from_calendar_date(2020, Month::January, 1)?
);
```

# format_description in time::macros - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/macros/macro.format_description.html

`format_description!() { /* proc-macro */ }`**crate feature**only.

`macros` and (crate features `formatting` or `parsing`)## Expand description

Equivalent of performing [ format_description::parse()](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/fn.parse.html) at compile time.

Using the macro instead of the function results in a static slice rather than a
[ Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html), such that it can be used in

`#![no_alloc]` situations. For
readability, you can use [as the type.](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/type.StaticFormatDescription.html)

`StaticFormatDescription`The resulting expression can be used in `const` or `static` declarations, and implements
the sealed traits required for both formatting and parsing.

```
assert_eq!(
    format_description!("[hour]:[minute]:[second]"),
    format_description::parse_borrowed::<2>("[hour]:[minute]:[second]")?
);
```
The syntax accepted by this macro is the same as [ format_description::parse()](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/fn.parse.html), which can
be found in

[the book](https://time-rs.github.io/book/api/format-description.html).

# offset in time::macros - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/macros/macro.offset.html

`offset!() { /* proc-macro */ }`Available on

**crate feature**only.`macros`## Expand description

Construct a [ UtcOffset](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.UtcOffset.html) with a statically known value.

The resulting expression can be used in `const` or `static` declarations.

A sign and the hour must be provided; minutes and seconds default to zero. `UTC` (both
uppercase and lowercase) is also allowed.

```
assert_eq!(offset!(UTC), UtcOffset::from_hms(0, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(utc), UtcOffset::from_hms(0, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(+0), UtcOffset::from_hms(0, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(+1), UtcOffset::from_hms(1, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(-1), UtcOffset::from_hms(-1, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(+1:30), UtcOffset::from_hms(1, 30, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(-1:30), UtcOffset::from_hms(-1, -30, 0)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(+1:30:59), UtcOffset::from_hms(1, 30, 59)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(-1:30:59), UtcOffset::from_hms(-1, -30, -59)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(+23:59:59), UtcOffset::from_hms(23, 59, 59)?);
assert_eq!(offset!(-23:59:59), UtcOffset::from_hms(-23, -59, -59)?);
```

# time in time::macros - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/macros/macro.time.html

`time!() { /* proc-macro */ }`**crate feature**only.

`macros`## Expand description

Construct a [ Time](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Time.html) with a statically known value.

The resulting expression can be used in `const` or `static` declarations.

Hours and minutes must be provided, while seconds defaults to zero. AM/PM is allowed (either uppercase or lowercase). Any number of subsecond digits may be provided (though any past nine will be discarded).

All components are validated at compile-time. An error will be raised if any value is invalid.

```
assert_eq!(time!(0:00), Time::from_hms(0, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(time!(1:02:03), Time::from_hms(1, 2, 3)?);
assert_eq!(
    time!(1:02:03.004_005_006),
    Time::from_hms_nano(1, 2, 3, 4_005_006)?
);
assert_eq!(time!(12:00 am), Time::from_hms(0, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(time!(1:02:03 am), Time::from_hms(1, 2, 3)?);
assert_eq!(
    time!(1:02:03.004_005_006 am),
    Time::from_hms_nano(1, 2, 3, 4_005_006)?
);
assert_eq!(time!(12 pm), Time::from_hms(12, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(time!(12:00 pm), Time::from_hms(12, 0, 0)?);
assert_eq!(time!(1:02:03 pm), Time::from_hms(13, 2, 3)?);
assert_eq!(
    time!(1:02:03.004_005_006 pm),
    Time::from_hms_nano(13, 2, 3, 4_005_006)?
);
```

[103](https://time-rs.github.io#103)impl [Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) for [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io#50-57) {
[104](https://time-rs.github.io#104)    #[inline]
[105](https://time-rs.github.io#105)    fn default() -> Self {
[106](https://time-rs.github.io#106)        Self::[ZERO](https://time-rs.github.io#247)
[107](https://time-rs.github.io#107)    }
[108](https://time-rs.github.io#108)}
[109](https://time-rs.github.io#109)
[110](https://time-rs.github.io#110)/// This is adapted from the [`std` implementation][std], which uses mostly bit
[111](https://time-rs.github.io#111)/// operations to ensure the highest precision:
[112](https://time-rs.github.io#112)///
[113](https://time-rs.github.io#113)/// Changes from `std` are marked and explained below.
[114](https://time-rs.github.io#114)///
[115](https://time-rs.github.io#115)/// [std]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/3a37c2f0523c87147b64f1b8099fc9df22e8c53e/library/core/src/time.rs#L1262-L1340
[116](https://time-rs.github.io#116)#[rustfmt::skip] // Skip `rustfmt` because it reformats the arguments of the macro weirdly.
[117](https://time-rs.github.io#117)macro_rules! try_from_secs {
[118](https://time-rs.github.io#118)    (
[119](https://time-rs.github.io#119)        secs = $secs: expr,
[120](https://time-rs.github.io#120)        mantissa_bits = $mant_bits: literal,
[121](https://time-rs.github.io#121)        exponent_bits = $exp_bits: literal,
[122](https://time-rs.github.io#122)        offset = $offset: literal,
[123](https://time-rs.github.io#123)        bits_ty = $bits_ty:ty,
[124](https://time-rs.github.io#124)        bits_ty_signed = $bits_ty_signed:ty,
[125](https://time-rs.github.io#125)        double_ty = $double_ty:ty,
[126](https://time-rs.github.io#126)        float_ty = $float_ty:ty,
[127](https://time-rs.github.io#127)    ) => {{
[128](https://time-rs.github.io#128)        'value: {
[129](https://time-rs.github.io#129)            const MIN_EXP: i16 = 1 - (1i16 << $exp_bits) / 2;
[130](https://time-rs.github.io#130)            const MANT_MASK: $bits_ty = (1 << $mant_bits) - 1;
[131](https://time-rs.github.io#131)            const EXP_MASK: $bits_ty = (1 << $exp_bits) - 1;
[132](https://time-rs.github.io#132)
[133](https://time-rs.github.io#133)            // Change from std: No error check for negative values necessary.
[134](https://time-rs.github.io#134)
[135](https://time-rs.github.io#135)            let bits = $secs.to_bits();
[136](https://time-rs.github.io#136)            let mant = (bits & MANT_MASK) | (MANT_MASK + 1);
[137](https://time-rs.github.io#137)            let exp = ((bits >> $mant_bits) & EXP_MASK) as i16 + MIN_EXP;
[138](https://time-rs.github.io#138)
[139](https://time-rs.github.io#139)            let (secs, nanos) = if exp < -31 {
[140](https://time-rs.github.io#140)                // the input represents less than 1ns and can not be rounded to it
[141](https://time-rs.github.io#141)                (0u64, 0u32)
[142](https://time-rs.github.io#142)            } else if exp < 0 {
[143](https://time-rs.github.io#143)                // the input is less than 1 second
[144](https://time-rs.github.io#144)                let t = (mant as $double_ty) << ($offset + exp);
[145](https://time-rs.github.io#145)                let nanos_offset = $mant_bits + $offset;
[146](https://time-rs.github.io#146)                #[allow(trivial_numeric_casts)]
[147](https://time-rs.github.io#147)                let nanos_tmp = Nanosecond::per_t::<u128>(Second) * t as u128;
[148](https://time-rs.github.io#148)                let nanos = (nanos_tmp >> nanos_offset) as u32;
[149](https://time-rs.github.io#149)
[150](https://time-rs.github.io#150)                let rem_mask = (1 << nanos_offset) - 1;
[151](https://time-rs.github.io#151)                let rem_msb_mask = 1 << (nanos_offset - 1);
[152](https://time-rs.github.io#152)                let rem = nanos_tmp & rem_mask;
[153](https://time-rs.github.io#153)                let is_tie = rem == rem_msb_mask;
[154](https://time-rs.github.io#154)                let is_even = (nanos & 1) == 0;
[155](https://time-rs.github.io#155)                let rem_msb = nanos_tmp & rem_msb_mask == 0;
[156](https://time-rs.github.io#156)                let add_ns = !(rem_msb || (is_even && is_tie));
[157](https://time-rs.github.io#157)
[158](https://time-rs.github.io#158)                // f32 does not have enough precision to trigger the second branch
[159](https://time-rs.github.io#159)                // since it can not represent numbers between 0.999_999_940_395 and 1.0.
[160](https://time-rs.github.io#160)                let nanos = nanos + add_ns as u32;
[161](https://time-rs.github.io#161)                if ($mant_bits == 23) || (nanos != Nanosecond::per_t::<u32>(Second)) {
[162](https://time-rs.github.io#162)                    (0, nanos)
[163](https://time-rs.github.io#163)                } else {
[164](https://time-rs.github.io#164)                    (1, 0)
[165](https://time-rs.github.io#165)                }
[166](https://time-rs.github.io#166)            } else if exp < $mant_bits {
[167](https://time-rs.github.io#167)                #[allow(trivial_numeric_casts)]
[168](https://time-rs.github.io#168)                let secs = (mant >> ($mant_bits - exp)) as u64;
[169](https://time-rs.github.io#169)                let t = ((mant << exp) & MANT_MASK) as $double_ty;
[170](https://time-rs.github.io#170)                let nanos_offset = $mant_bits;
[171](https://time-rs.github.io#171)                let nanos_tmp = Nanosecond::per_t::<$double_ty>(Second) * t;
[172](https://time-rs.github.io#172)                let nanos = (nanos_tmp >> nanos_offset) as u32;
[173](https://time-rs.github.io#173)
[174](https://time-rs.github.io#174)                let rem_mask = (1 << nanos_offset) - 1;
[175](https://time-rs.github.io#175)                let rem_msb_mask = 1 << (nanos_offset - 1);
[176](https://time-rs.github.io#176)                let rem = nanos_tmp & rem_mask;
[177](https://time-rs.github.io#177)                let is_tie = rem == rem_msb_mask;
[178](https://time-rs.github.io#178)                let is_even = (nanos & 1) == 0;
[179](https://time-rs.github.io#179)                let rem_msb = nanos_tmp & rem_msb_mask == 0;
[180](https://time-rs.github.io#180)                let add_ns = !(rem_msb || (is_even && is_tie));
[181](https://time-rs.github.io#181)
[182](https://time-rs.github.io#182)                // f32 does not have enough precision to trigger the second branch.
[183](https://time-rs.github.io#183)                // For example, it can not represent numbers between 1.999_999_880...
[184](https://time-rs.github.io#184)                // and 2.0. Bigger values result in even smaller precision of the
[185](https://time-rs.github.io#185)                // fractional part.
[186](https://time-rs.github.io#186)                let nanos = nanos + add_ns as u32;
[187](https://time-rs.github.io#187)                if ($mant_bits == 23) || (nanos != Nanosecond::per_t::<u32>(Second)) {
[188](https://time-rs.github.io#188)                    (secs, nanos)
[189](https://time-rs.github.io#189)                } else {
[190](https://time-rs.github.io#190)                    (secs + 1, 0)
[191](https://time-rs.github.io#191)                }
[192](https://time-rs.github.io#192)            } else if exp < 63 {
[193](https://time-rs.github.io#193)                // Change from std: The exponent here is 63 instead of 64,
[194](https://time-rs.github.io#194)                // because i64::MAX + 1 is 2^63.
[195](https://time-rs.github.io#195)
[196](https://time-rs.github.io#196)                // the input has no fractional part
[197](https://time-rs.github.io#197)                #[allow(trivial_numeric_casts)]
[198](https://time-rs.github.io#198)                let secs = (mant as u64) << (exp - $mant_bits);
[199](https://time-rs.github.io#199)                (secs, 0)
[200](https://time-rs.github.io#200)            } else if bits == (i64::MIN as $float_ty).to_bits() {
[201](https://time-rs.github.io#201)                // Change from std: Signed integers are asymmetrical in that
[202](https://time-rs.github.io#202)                // iN::MIN is -iN::MAX - 1. So for example i8 covers the
[203](https://time-rs.github.io#203)                // following numbers -128..=127. The check above (exp < 63)
[204](https://time-rs.github.io#204)                // doesn't cover i64::MIN as that is -2^63, so we have this
[205](https://time-rs.github.io#205)                // additional case to handle the asymmetry of iN::MIN.
[206](https://time-rs.github.io#206)                break 'value Ok(Self::new_ranged_unchecked(i64::MIN, Nanoseconds::new_static::<0>()));
[207](https://time-rs.github.io#207)            } else if $secs.is_nan() {
[208](https://time-rs.github.io#208)                // Change from std: std doesn't differentiate between the error
[209](https://time-rs.github.io#209)                // cases.
[210](https://time-rs.github.io#210)                break 'value Err(FloatConstructorError::Nan);
[211](https://time-rs.github.io#211)            } else if $secs.is_sign_negative() {
[212](https://time-rs.github.io#212)                break 'value Err(FloatConstructorError::NegOverflow);
[213](https://time-rs.github.io#213)            } else {
[214](https://time-rs.github.io#214)                break 'value Err(FloatConstructorError::PosOverflow);
[215](https://time-rs.github.io#215)            };
[216](https://time-rs.github.io#216)
[217](https://time-rs.github.io#217)            // Change from std: All the code is mostly unmodified in that it
[218](https://time-rs.github.io#218)            // simply calculates an unsigned integer. Here we extract the sign
[219](https://time-rs.github.io#219)            // bit and assign it to the number. We basically manually do two's
[220](https://time-rs.github.io#220)            // complement here, we could also use an if and just negate the
[221](https://time-rs.github.io#221)            // numbers based on the sign, but it turns out to be quite a bit
[222](https://time-rs.github.io#222)            // slower.
[223](https://time-rs.github.io#223)            let mask = (bits as $bits_ty_signed) >> ($mant_bits + $exp_bits);
[224](https://time-rs.github.io#224)            #[allow(trivial_numeric_casts)]
[225](https://time-rs.github.io#225)            let secs_signed = ((secs as i64) ^ (mask as i64)) - (mask as i64);
[226](https://time-rs.github.io#226)            #[allow(trivial_numeric_casts)]
[227](https://time-rs.github.io#227)            let nanos_signed = ((nanos as i32) ^ (mask as i32)) - (mask as i32);
[228](https://time-rs.github.io#228)            // Safety: `nanos_signed` is in range.
[229](https://time-rs.github.io#229)            Ok(unsafe { Self::new_unchecked(secs_signed, nanos_signed) })
[230](https://time-rs.github.io#230)        }
[231](https://time-rs.github.io#231)    }};
[232](https://time-rs.github.io#232)}

[344](https://time-rs.github.io#344)    /// Check if a duration is positive.
[345](https://time-rs.github.io#345)    ///
[346](https://time-rs.github.io#346)    /// ```rust
[347](https://time-rs.github.io#347)    /// # use time::ext::NumericalDuration;
[348](https://time-rs.github.io#348)    /// assert!(1.seconds().is_positive());
[349](https://time-rs.github.io#349)    /// assert!(!0.seconds().is_positive());
[350](https://time-rs.github.io#350)    /// assert!(!(-1).seconds().is_positive());
[351](https://time-rs.github.io#351)    /// ```

[371](https://time-rs.github.io#371)            [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) => Self::[MAX](https://time-rs.github.io#317),
[372](https://time-rs.github.io#372)        }

[394](https://time-rs.github.io#394)    /// # Safety
[395](https://time-rs.github.io#395)    ///
[396](https://time-rs.github.io#396)    /// - `nanoseconds` must be in the range `-999_999_999..=999_999_999`.
[397](https://time-rs.github.io#397)    ///

[399](https://time-rs.github.io#399)    /// not a safety invariant.
[400](https://time-rs.github.io#400)    #[inline]

[402](https://time-rs.github.io#402)    pub(crate) const unsafe fn new_unchecked(seconds: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), nanoseconds: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> Self {
[403](https://time-rs.github.io#403)        Self::[new_ranged_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#413-425)(
[404](https://time-rs.github.io#404)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#402),
[405](https://time-rs.github.io#405)            // Safety: The caller must uphold the safety invariants.
[406](https://time-rs.github.io#406)            unsafe { [Nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#39-40)::new_unchecked([nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#402)) },
[407](https://time-rs.github.io#407)        )
[408](https://time-rs.github.io#408)    }
[409](https://time-rs.github.io#409)
[410](https://time-rs.github.io#410)    /// Create a new `Duration` without checking the validity of the components.
[411](https://time-rs.github.io#411)    #[inline]
[412](https://time-rs.github.io#412)    #[track_caller]
[413](https://time-rs.github.io#413)    pub(crate) const fn new_ranged_unchecked(seconds: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), nanoseconds: [Nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#39-40)) -> Self {
[414](https://time-rs.github.io#414)        if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#413) < 0 {
[415](https://time-rs.github.io#415)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(nanoseconds.get() <= 0);
[416](https://time-rs.github.io#416)        } else if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#413) > 0 {
[417](https://time-rs.github.io#417)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(nanoseconds.get() >= 0);
[418](https://time-rs.github.io#418)        }
[419](https://time-rs.github.io#419)
[420](https://time-rs.github.io#420)        Self {
[421](https://time-rs.github.io#421)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#413),
[422](https://time-rs.github.io#422)            [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#413),
[423](https://time-rs.github.io#423)            _padding: Padding::[Optimize](https://time-rs.github.io#35),
[424](https://time-rs.github.io#424)        }
[425](https://time-rs.github.io#425)    }

[427](https://time-rs.github.io#427)    /// Create a new `Duration` with the provided seconds and nanoseconds. If nanoseconds is at
[428](https://time-rs.github.io#428)    /// least ±10<sup>9</sup>, it will wrap to the number of seconds.
[429](https://time-rs.github.io#429)    ///
[430](https://time-rs.github.io#430)    /// ```rust
[431](https://time-rs.github.io#431)    /// # use time::{Duration, ext::NumericalDuration};
[432](https://time-rs.github.io#432)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::new(1, 0), 1.seconds());
[433](https://time-rs.github.io#433)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::new(-1, 0), (-1).seconds());
[434](https://time-rs.github.io#434)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::new(1, 2_000_000_000), 3.seconds());
[435](https://time-rs.github.io#435)    /// ```
[436](https://time-rs.github.io#436)    ///
[437](https://time-rs.github.io#437)    /// # Panics
[438](https://time-rs.github.io#438)    ///
[439](https://time-rs.github.io#439)    /// This may panic if an overflow occurs.
[440](https://time-rs.github.io#440)    #[inline]
[441](https://time-rs.github.io#441)    #[track_caller]
[442](https://time-rs.github.io#442)    pub const fn new(mut seconds: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), mut nanoseconds: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> Self {
[443](https://time-rs.github.io#443)        [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) = [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442)
[444](https://time-rs.github.io#444)            .[checked_add](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i64.html#method.checked_add)([nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html) / [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)))
[445](https://time-rs.github.io#445)            .[expect](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.expect)("overflow constructing `time::Duration`");
[446](https://time-rs.github.io#446)        [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) %= [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[447](https://time-rs.github.io#447)
[448](https://time-rs.github.io#448)        if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) > 0 && [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) < 0 {
[449](https://time-rs.github.io#449)            // `seconds` cannot overflow here because it is positive.
[450](https://time-rs.github.io#450)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) -= 1;
[451](https://time-rs.github.io#451)            [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) += [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[452](https://time-rs.github.io#452)        } else if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) < 0 && [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) > 0 {
[453](https://time-rs.github.io#453)            // `seconds` cannot overflow here because it is negative.
[454](https://time-rs.github.io#454)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) += 1;
[455](https://time-rs.github.io#455)            [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442) -= [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[456](https://time-rs.github.io#456)        }
[457](https://time-rs.github.io#457)
[458](https://time-rs.github.io#458)        // Safety: `nanoseconds` is in range due to the modulus above.
[459](https://time-rs.github.io#459)        unsafe { Self::[new_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#402-408)([seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442), [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#442)) }
[460](https://time-rs.github.io#460)    }
[461](https://time-rs.github.io#461)
[462](https://time-rs.github.io#462)    /// Create a new `Duration` with the provided seconds and nanoseconds.
[463](https://time-rs.github.io#463)    #[inline]
[464](https://time-rs.github.io#464)    pub(crate) const fn new_ranged(mut seconds: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), mut nanoseconds: [Nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#39-40)) -> Self {
[465](https://time-rs.github.io#465)        if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) > 0 && [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464).get() < 0 {
[466](https://time-rs.github.io#466)            // `seconds` cannot overflow here because it is positive.
[467](https://time-rs.github.io#467)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) -= 1;
[468](https://time-rs.github.io#468)            // Safety: `nanoseconds` is negative with a maximum of 999,999,999, so adding a billion
[469](https://time-rs.github.io#469)            // to it is guaranteed to result in an in-range value.
[470](https://time-rs.github.io#470)            [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) = unsafe {
[471](https://time-rs.github.io#471)                [Nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#39-40)::new_unchecked([nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464).get() + [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)))
[472](https://time-rs.github.io#472)            };
[473](https://time-rs.github.io#473)        } else if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) < 0 && [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464).get() > 0 {
[474](https://time-rs.github.io#474)            // `seconds` cannot overflow here because it is negative.
[475](https://time-rs.github.io#475)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) += 1;
[476](https://time-rs.github.io#476)            // Safety: `nanoseconds` is positive with a minimum of -999,999,999, so subtracting a
[477](https://time-rs.github.io#477)            // billion from it is guaranteed to result in an in-range value.
[478](https://time-rs.github.io#478)            [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464) = unsafe {
[479](https://time-rs.github.io#479)                [Nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#39-40)::new_unchecked([nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464).get() - [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)))
[480](https://time-rs.github.io#480)            };
[481](https://time-rs.github.io#481)        }
[482](https://time-rs.github.io#482)
[483](https://time-rs.github.io#483)        Self::[new_ranged_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#413-425)([seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464), [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#464))
[484](https://time-rs.github.io#484)    }

[666](https://time-rs.github.io#666)    /// Creates a new `Duration` from the specified number of seconds
[667](https://time-rs.github.io#667)    /// represented as `f64`. Any values that are out of bounds are saturated at
[668](https://time-rs.github.io#668)    /// the minimum or maximum respectively. `NaN` gets turned into a `Duration`
[669](https://time-rs.github.io#669)    /// of 0 seconds.
[670](https://time-rs.github.io#670)    ///
[671](https://time-rs.github.io#671)    /// ```rust
[672](https://time-rs.github.io#672)    /// # use time::{Duration, ext::NumericalDuration};
[673](https://time-rs.github.io#673)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(0.5), 0.5.seconds());
[674](https://time-rs.github.io#674)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(-0.5), (-0.5).seconds());
[675](https://time-rs.github.io#675)    /// assert_eq!(
[676](https://time-rs.github.io#676)    ///     Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::NAN),
[677](https://time-rs.github.io#677)    ///     Duration::new(0, 0),
[678](https://time-rs.github.io#678)    /// );
[679](https://time-rs.github.io#679)    /// assert_eq!(
[680](https://time-rs.github.io#680)    ///     Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::NEG_INFINITY),
[681](https://time-rs.github.io#681)    ///     Duration::MIN,
[682](https://time-rs.github.io#682)    /// );
[683](https://time-rs.github.io#683)    /// assert_eq!(
[684](https://time-rs.github.io#684)    ///     Duration::saturating_seconds_f64(f64::INFINITY),
[685](https://time-rs.github.io#685)    ///     Duration::MAX,
[686](https://time-rs.github.io#686)    /// );
[687](https://time-rs.github.io#687)    /// ```
[688](https://time-rs.github.io#688)    #[inline]
[689](https://time-rs.github.io#689)    pub const fn saturating_seconds_f64(seconds: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> Self {
[690](https://time-rs.github.io#690)        match Self::[try_seconds_f64](https://time-rs.github.io#585-596)([seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#689)) {
[691](https://time-rs.github.io#691)            [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(duration) => [duration](https://time-rs.github.io#691),
[692](https://time-rs.github.io#692)            [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(FloatConstructorError::[Nan](https://time-rs.github.io#24)) => Self::[ZERO](https://time-rs.github.io#247),
[693](https://time-rs.github.io#693)            [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(FloatConstructorError::[NegOverflow](https://time-rs.github.io#25)) => Self::[MIN](https://time-rs.github.io#314),
[694](https://time-rs.github.io#694)            [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(FloatConstructorError::[PosOverflow](https://time-rs.github.io#26)) => Self::[MAX](https://time-rs.github.io#317),

[770](https://time-rs.github.io#770)    /// Create a new `Duration` with the given number of milliseconds.
[771](https://time-rs.github.io#771)    ///
[772](https://time-rs.github.io#772)    /// ```rust
[773](https://time-rs.github.io#773)    /// # use time::{Duration, ext::NumericalDuration};
[774](https://time-rs.github.io#774)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::milliseconds(1), 1_000.microseconds());
[775](https://time-rs.github.io#775)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::milliseconds(-1), (-1_000).microseconds());
[776](https://time-rs.github.io#776)    /// ```
[777](https://time-rs.github.io#777)    #[inline]
[778](https://time-rs.github.io#778)    pub const fn milliseconds(milliseconds: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)) -> Self {
[779](https://time-rs.github.io#779)        // Safety: `nanoseconds` is guaranteed to be in range because of the modulus.
[780](https://time-rs.github.io#780)        unsafe {
[781](https://time-rs.github.io#781)            Self::[new_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#402-408)(
[782](https://time-rs.github.io#782)                [milliseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#778) / [Millisecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Millisecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Millisecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html)),
[783](https://time-rs.github.io#783)                ([milliseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#778) % [Millisecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Millisecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Millisecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html))

[826](https://time-rs.github.io#826)    /// Create a new `Duration` with the given number of nanoseconds.
[827](https://time-rs.github.io#827)    ///
[828](https://time-rs.github.io#828)    /// ```rust

[833](https://time-rs.github.io#833)    /// );
[834](https://time-rs.github.io#834)    /// ```
[835](https://time-rs.github.io#835)    ///
[836](https://time-rs.github.io#836)    /// # Panics
[837](https://time-rs.github.io#837)    ///
[838](https://time-rs.github.io#838)    /// This may panic if an overflow occurs. This may happen because the input range cannot be
[839](https://time-rs.github.io#839)    /// fully mapped to the output.
[840](https://time-rs.github.io#840)    #[inline]
[841](https://time-rs.github.io#841)    #[track_caller]
[842](https://time-rs.github.io#842)    pub const fn nanoseconds_i128(nanoseconds: [i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html)) -> Self {
[843](https://time-rs.github.io#843)        let seconds = [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#842) / [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[844](https://time-rs.github.io#844)        let nanoseconds = [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#842) % [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[845](https://time-rs.github.io#845)
[846](https://time-rs.github.io#846)        if [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#843) > [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)::[MAX](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i64.html#associatedconstant.MAX) as [i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html) || [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#843) < [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)::[MIN](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.i64.html#associatedconstant.MIN) as [i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html) {
[847](https://time-rs.github.io#847)            [panic!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.panic.html)("overflow constructing `time::Duration`");
[848](https://time-rs.github.io#848)        }
[849](https://time-rs.github.io#849)
[850](https://time-rs.github.io#850)        // Safety: `nanoseconds` is guaranteed to be in range because of the modulus above.
[851](https://time-rs.github.io#851)        unsafe { Self::[new_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#402-408)([seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#843) as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#844) as [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) }
[852](https://time-rs.github.io#852)    }

[1093](https://time-rs.github.io#1093)    /// Computes `self * rhs`, returning `None` if an overflow occurred.
[1094](https://time-rs.github.io#1094)    ///
[1095](https://time-rs.github.io#1095)    /// ```rust
[1096](https://time-rs.github.io#1096)    /// # use time::{Duration, ext::NumericalDuration};
[1097](https://time-rs.github.io#1097)    /// assert_eq!(5.seconds().checked_mul(2), Some(10.seconds()));
[1098](https://time-rs.github.io#1098)    /// assert_eq!(5.seconds().checked_mul(-2), Some((-10).seconds()));
[1099](https://time-rs.github.io#1099)    /// assert_eq!(5.seconds().checked_mul(0), Some(0.seconds()));
[1100](https://time-rs.github.io#1100)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::MAX.checked_mul(2), None);
[1101](https://time-rs.github.io#1101)    /// assert_eq!(Duration::MIN.checked_mul(2), None);
[1102](https://time-rs.github.io#1102)    /// ```
[1103](https://time-rs.github.io#1103)    #[inline]
[1104](https://time-rs.github.io#1104)    pub const fn checked_mul(self, rhs: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self> {
[1105](https://time-rs.github.io#1105)        // Multiply nanoseconds as i64, because it cannot overflow that way.
[1106](https://time-rs.github.io#1106)        let total_nanos = [self](https://time-rs.github.io#1104).nanoseconds.get() as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html) * [rhs](https://time-rs.github.io#1104) as [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html);
[1107](https://time-rs.github.io#1107)        let extra_secs = [total_nanos](https://time-rs.github.io#1106) / [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html));
[1108](https://time-rs.github.io#1108)        let nanoseconds = ([total_nanos](https://time-rs.github.io#1106) % [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Nanosecond.html)::[per_t](https://time-rs.github.io/time_core/unit/struct.Nanosecond.html#method.per_t)::<[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)>([Second](https://time-rs.github.io/time/convert/struct.Second.html))) as [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html);
[1109](https://time-rs.github.io#1109)        let seconds = [const_try_opt!](https://time-rs.github.io/internal_macros.rs.html#201-211)(
[1110](https://time-rs.github.io#1110)            const_try_opt!(self.seconds.checked_mul(rhs as i64)).checked_add(extra_secs)
[1111](https://time-rs.github.io#1111)        );
[1112](https://time-rs.github.io#1112)
[1113](https://time-rs.github.io#1113)        // Safety: `nanoseconds` is guaranteed to be in range because of the modulus above.
[1114](https://time-rs.github.io#1114)        unsafe { [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(Self::[new_unchecked](https://time-rs.github.io#402-408)([seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#1109), [nanoseconds](https://time-rs.github.io#1108))) }
[1115](https://time-rs.github.io#1115)    }

[1117](https://time-rs.github.io#1117)    /// Computes `self / rhs`, returning `None` if `rhs == 0` or if the result would overflow.
[1118](https://time-rs.github.io#1118)    ///
[1119](https://time-rs.github.io#1119)    /// ```rust

[1125](https://time-rs.github.io#1125)    #[inline]
[1126](https://time-rs.github.io#1126)    pub const fn checked_div(self, rhs: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self> {

[1128](https://time-rs.github.io#1128)            [const_try_opt!](https://time-rs.github.io/internal_macros.rs.html#201-211)(self.seconds.checked_div(rhs as i64)),

[1243](https://time-rs.github.io#1243)    /// Computes `self * rhs`, saturating if an overflow occurred.

[1311](https://time-rs.github.io#1311)///

[159](https://time-rs.github.io#159)            _ => {
[160](https://time-rs.github.io#160)                hint::[cold_path](https://time-rs.github.io/hint.rs.html#6)();
[161](https://time-rs.github.io#161)                return [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(error::[ComponentRange](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range.rs.html#11-17)::[conditional](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range.rs.html#31-36)("day"));
[162](https://time-rs.github.io#162)            }
[163](https://time-rs.github.io#163)        }
[164](https://time-rs.github.io#164)
[165](https://time-rs.github.io#165)        // Safety: `ordinal` is not zero and `is_leap_year` is correct.
[166](https://time-rs.github.io#166)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(unsafe {
[167](https://time-rs.github.io#167)            Self::[from_parts](https://time-rs.github.io#98-111)(

[170](https://time-rs.github.io#170)                [DAYS_CUMULATIVE_COMMON_LEAP](https://time-rs.github.io#148-151)[[is_leap_year](https://time-rs.github.io#155) as [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)][[month](https://time-rs.github.io#144) as [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html) - 1] + [day](https://time-rs.github.io#145) as [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html),
[171](https://time-rs.github.io#171)            )

[275](https://time-rs.github.io#275)    /// Create a `Date` from the Julian day.
