[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/date.rs.html#554-563)#### pub const fn [to_iso_week_date](https://time-rs.github.io#method.to_iso_week_date)(self) -> ([i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), [Weekday](https://time-rs.github.io/weekday/enum.Weekday.html))

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/date.rs.html#554-563)

#### pub const fn [to_iso_week_date](https://time-rs.github.io#method.to_iso_week_date)(self) -> ([i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), [Weekday](https://time-rs.github.io/weekday/enum.Weekday.html))

Get the ISO 8601 year, week number, and weekday.

```
assert_eq!(date!(2019-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2019, 1, Tuesday));
assert_eq!(date!(2019-10-04).to_iso_week_date(), (2019, 40, Friday));
assert_eq!(date!(2020-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 1, Wednesday));
assert_eq!(date!(2020-12-31).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 53, Thursday));
assert_eq!(date!(2021-01-01).to_iso_week_date(), (2020, 53, Friday));
```
Get the weekday.

```
assert_eq!(date!(2019-01-01).weekday(), Tuesday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-02-01).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-03-01).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-04-01).weekday(), Monday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-05-01).weekday(), Wednesday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-06-01).weekday(), Saturday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-07-01).weekday(), Monday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-08-01).weekday(), Thursday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-09-01).weekday(), Sunday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-10-01).weekday(), Tuesday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-11-01).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(date!(2019-12-01).weekday(), Sunday);
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/date.rs.html#809-837)

#### pub const fn [checked_add](https://time-rs.github.io#method.checked_add)(self, duration: [Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/duration/struct.Duration.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

Computes `self + duration`, returning `None` if an overflow occurred.

```
assert_eq!(Date::MAX.checked_add(1.days()), None);
assert_eq!(Date::MIN.checked_add((-2).days()), None);
assert_eq!(
    date!(2020-12-31).checked_add(2.days()),
    Some(date!(2021-01-02))
);
```
[§](https://time-rs.github.io#note)Note

This function only takes whole days into account.

# Duration in time::duration - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/duration/struct.Duration.html

Struct Duration  Copy item path  Source  #[repr(C)]

pub struct Duration {
    seconds: i64 ,
    nanoseconds: ri32<{ _ }, { _ }>,
    _padding: Padding ,
}Expand description A span of time with nanosecond precision.

Each `Duration` is composed of a whole number of seconds and a fractional part represented in
nanoseconds.

This implementation allows for negative durations, unlike `core::time::Duration`

Number of nanoseconds within the second. The sign always matches the `seconds` field.

Equivalent to `0.seconds()`.

}## Expand description

A unified error type for anything returned by a method in the time crate.

This can be used when you either don’t know or don’t care about the exact error returned.
`Result<_, time::Error>` (or its alias `time::Result<_>`) will work in these situations.

# Instant in time::instant - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/instant/struct.Instant.html

`#[doc(hidden)]#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Instant(pub `[Instant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.Instant.html));import `std::time::Instant` and `time::ext::InstantExt` instead

**crate feature**only.

`std`## Expand description

A measurement of a monotonically non-decreasing clock. Opaque and useful only with [ Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/duration/struct.Duration.html).

Instants are always guaranteed to be no less than any previously measured instant when created, and are often useful for tasks such as measuring benchmarks or timing how long an operation takes.

Note, however, that instants are not guaranteed to be **steady**. In other words, each tick of
the underlying clock may not be the same length (e.g. some seconds may be longer than others).
An instant may jump forwards or experience time dilation (slow down or speed up), but it will
never go backwards.

Instants are opaque types that can only be compared to one another. There is no method to get “the number of seconds” from an instant. Instead, it only allows measuring the duration between two instants (or comparing two instants).

This implementation allows for operations with signed [ Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/duration/struct.Duration.html)s, but is otherwise identical
to

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.Instant.html)

assert_eq!(

// Let's see what time Sydney's new year's celebration is in New York and Los Angeles.
// Construct midnight on new year's in Sydney.
let sydney = datetime!(2000-01-01 0:00 +11);
let new_york = sydney.to_offset(offset!(-5));
let los_angeles = sydney.to_offset(offset!(-8));
assert_eq!(sydney.hour(), 0);
assert_eq!(new_york.hour(), 8);
assert_eq!(los_angeles.hour(), 5);

Create an `OffsetDateTime` from the provided Unix timestamp. Calling `.offset()` on the
resulting value is guaranteed to return UTC.

```
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(0),
    Ok(OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH),
);
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(1_546_300_800),
    Ok(datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00 UTC)),
);
```

    (2020, 53, Thursday)

assert_eq!(datetime.checked_add((-2).days()), None);
let datetime = Date::MAX.midnight().assume_offset(offset!(+10));
assert_eq!(datetime.checked_add(2.days()), None);

    Some(datetime!(2019-11-26 18:30 +10))
);
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1157-1159)

#### pub const fn [replace_time](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_time)(self, time: [Time](https://time-rs.github.io/time/struct.Time.html)) -> Self

Replace the time, which is assumed to be in the stored offset. The date and offset components are unchanged.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 5:00 UTC).replace_time(time!(12:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 UTC)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 -5).replace_time(time!(7:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 7:00 -5)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 0:00 +1).replace_time(time!(12:00)),
    datetime!(2020-01-01 12:00 +1)
);
```

    Ok(datetime!(2019-02-18 12:00 +01))
);

`formatting`[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1568-1574)**crate feature **`parsing` only.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1568-1574)

**crate feature**only.

`parsing`Parse an `OffsetDateTime` from the input using the provided [format
description](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/index.html) and default values.

```
let format = format_description!("[year]-[month]-[day] [hour]:[minute]");
let defaults = Parsed::new()
    .with_offset_hour(0).expect("0 is a valid offset hour")
    .with_offset_minute_signed(0).expect("0 is a valid offset minute");
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::parse_with_defaults(b"2020-01-02 03:04", &format, defaults)?,
    datetime!(2020-01-02 03:04 +0:00)
);
```
[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1581-1597)#### pub(crate) const fn [is_valid_leap_second_stand_in](https://time-rs.github.io#method.is_valid_leap_second_stand_in)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

**crate feature **`parsing` only.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/offset_date_time.rs.html#1581-1597)

#### pub(crate) const fn [is_valid_leap_second_stand_in](https://time-rs.github.io#method.is_valid_leap_second_stand_in)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

**crate feature**only.

`parsing`A helper method to check if the `OffsetDateTime` is a valid representation of a leap second.
Leap seconds, when parsed, are represented as the preceding nanosecond. However, leap
seconds can only occur as the last second of a month UTC.

# PrimitiveDateTime in time::primitive_date_time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/primitive_date_time/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html

## Expand description

Combined date and time.

## Fields[§](https://time-rs.github.io#fields)

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.time)

`time: `[Time](https://time-rs.github.io/time/struct.Time.html)**little-endian**only.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.date)

`date: `[Date](https://time-rs.github.io/date/struct.Date.html)**little-endian**only.

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

The smallest value that can be represented by `PrimitiveDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

- With `large-dates`disabled it is equal to`-9999-01-01 00:00:00.0`
- With `large-dates`enabled it is equal to`-999999-01-01 00:00:00.0`

The largest value that can be represented by `PrimitiveDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

- With `large-dates`disabled it is equal to`9999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`
- With `large-dates`enabled it is equal to`999999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`

Provide a representation of `PrimitiveDateTime` as a `i128`. This value can be used for
equality, hashing, and ordering.

**Note**: This value is explicitly signed, so do not cast this to or treat this as an
unsigned integer. Doing so will lead to incorrect results for values with differing
signs.

Get the ISO week number.

The returned value will always be in the range `1..=53`.

Get the ISO 8601 year, week number, and weekday.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 1, Tuesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2019-10-04 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 40, Friday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 1, Wednesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2020-12-31 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Thursday)
);
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2021-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Friday)
);
```
Get the weekday.

```
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00).weekday(), Tuesday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-02-01 0:00).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-03-01 0:00).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-04-01 0:00).weekday(), Monday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-05-01 0:00).weekday(), Wednesday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-06-01 0:00).weekday(), Saturday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-07-01 0:00).weekday(), Monday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-08-01 0:00).weekday(), Thursday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-09-01 0:00).weekday(), Sunday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-10-01 0:00).weekday(), Tuesday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-11-01 0:00).weekday(), Friday);
assert_eq!(datetime!(2019-12-01 0:00).weekday(), Sunday);
```

#### pub const fn [assume_utc](https://time-rs.github.io#method.assume_utc)(self) -> [OffsetDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/offset_date_time/struct.OffsetDateTime.html)

Assuming that the existing `PrimitiveDateTime` represents a moment in UTC, return an
[ OffsetDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/offset_date_time/struct.OffsetDateTime.html).

**Note**: You may want a [ UtcDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/utc_date_time/struct.UtcDateTime.html) instead, which can be obtained with the

[method.](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html#method.as_utc)

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/primitive_date_time.rs.html#769-774)#### pub const fn [replace_year](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_year)(self, year: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ComponentRange](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range/struct.ComponentRange.html)>

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/primitive_date_time.rs.html#769-774)

#### pub const fn [replace_year](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_year)(self, year: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ComponentRange](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range/struct.ComponentRange.html)>

Replace the year. The month and day will be unchanged.

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00).replace_year(2019),
    Ok(datetime!(2019-02-18 12:00))
);
assert!(datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00).replace_year(-1_000_000_000).is_err()); // -1_000_000_000 isn't a valid year
assert!(datetime!(2022-02-18 12:00).replace_year(1_000_000_000).is_err()); // 1_000_000_000 isn't a valid year
```

# Time in time::time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/time/struct.Time.html

```
pub struct Time {
    nanosecond: ru32<0, { _ }>,
    second: ru8<0, { _ }>,
    minute: ru8<0, { _ }>,
    hour: ru8<0, { _ }>,
    padding:
```
[Padding](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.Padding.html),
}## Expand description

The clock time within a given date. Nanosecond precision.

All minutes are assumed to have exactly 60 seconds; no attempt is made to handle leap seconds (either positive or negative).

When comparing two `Time`s, they are assumed to be in the same calendar date.

## Fields[§](https://time-rs.github.io#fields)

# Timestamp in time::timestamp - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/timestamp/struct.Timestamp.html

```
pub struct Timestamp {
    padding:
```
[Padding](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.Padding.html),
    nanoseconds: ru32<0, 999_999_999>,
    seconds: ri64<{ _ }, { _ }>,
}## Expand description

A Unix timestamp with nanosecond precision.

This type represents a point in time as a number of seconds and nanoseconds elapsed since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). Negative values represent times before the Unix epoch.

## Fields[§](https://time-rs.github.io#fields)

`padding: `[Padding](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.Padding.html)**little-endian**only.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.nanoseconds)

`nanoseconds: ru32<0, 999_999_999>`**little-endian**only.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.seconds)

`seconds: ri64<{ _ }, { _ }>`**little-endian**only.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#panics)Panics

This panics if the resulting date-time with the provided offset is outside the supported
range. Consider using [ checked_to_offset](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Timestamp.html#method.checked_to_offset) for a non-panicking
alternative.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/timestamp.rs.html#452-478)#### const fn [year_leap_ordinal](https://time-rs.github.io#method.year_leap_ordinal)(self) -> ([i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html))

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/timestamp.rs.html#452-478)

#### const fn [year_leap_ordinal](https://time-rs.github.io#method.year_leap_ordinal)(self) -> ([i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html), [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html))

Compute the year, leap year status, and ordinal day of the timestamp in UTC.

This algorithm is essentially identical to `Date::from_julian_day_unchecked`. Instead of
returning `Date`, it returns the components as a tuple. By not bitpacking the values, it
allows the compiler to see through the function boundary and better optimize methods.

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/timestamp.rs.html#1128-1131)#### pub const fn [replace_ordinal](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_ordinal)(self, ordinal: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ComponentRange](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range/struct.ComponentRange.html)>

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/timestamp.rs.html#1128-1131)

#### pub const fn [replace_ordinal](https://time-rs.github.io#method.replace_ordinal)(self, ordinal: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ComponentRange](https://time-rs.github.io/error/component_range/struct.ComponentRange.html)>

Replace the day of the year.

```
assert_eq!(
    timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(1),
    Ok(timestamp!(1_546_311_845))
);
assert!(timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(0).is_err()); // 0 isn't a valid day of the year
assert!(timestamp!(1_546_398_245).replace_ordinal(366).is_err()); // the timestamp is in 2019, which isn't a leap year
```

# UtcDateTime in time::utc_date_time - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/utc_date_time/struct.UtcDateTime.html

#[repr(transparent)]pub struct UtcDateTime {
    inner:
```
[PrimitiveDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/primitive_date_time/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html),
}## Expand description

A [ PrimitiveDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/primitive_date_time/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html) that is known to be UTC.

`UtcDateTime` is guaranteed to be ABI-compatible with [ PrimitiveDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/primitive_date_time/struct.PrimitiveDateTime.html), meaning that
transmuting from one to the other will not result in undefined behavior.

### impl [UtcDateTime](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.UtcDateTime.html)

The smallest value that can be represented by `UtcDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

- With `large-dates`disabled it is equal to`-9999-01-01 00:00:00.0`
- With `large-dates`enabled it is equal to`-999999-01-01 00:00:00.0`

The largest value that can be represented by `UtcDateTime`.

Depending on `large-dates` feature flag, value of this constant may vary.

- With `large-dates`disabled it is equal to`9999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`
- With `large-dates`enabled it is equal to`999999-12-31 23:59:59.999_999_999`

Create a `UtcDateTime` from the provided Unix timestamp.

```
assert_eq!(
    UtcDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(0),
    Ok(UtcDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH),
);
assert_eq!(
    UtcDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(1_546_300_800),
    Ok(utc_datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00)),
);
```
If you have a timestamp-nanosecond pair, you can use something along the lines of the following:

Convert the `UtcDateTime` from UTC to the provided [ UtcOffset](https://time-rs.github.io/utc_offset/struct.UtcOffset.html), returning an

`OffsetDateTime````
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2000-01-01 0:00)
        .to_offset(offset!(-1))
        .year(),
    1999,
);
// Construct midnight on new year's, UTC.
let utc = utc_datetime!(2000-01-01 0:00);
let new_york = utc.to_offset(offset!(-5));
let los_angeles = utc.to_offset(offset!(-8));
assert_eq!(utc.hour(), 0);
assert_eq!(new_york.hour(), 19);
assert_eq!(los_angeles.hour(), 16);
```
[§](https://time-rs.github.io#panics)Panics

This method panics if the local date-time in the new offset is outside the supported range.

Get the ISO 8601 year, week number, and weekday.

```
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2019-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 1, Tuesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2019-10-04 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2019, 40, Friday)
);
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2020-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 1, Wednesday)
);
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2020-12-31 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Thursday)
);
assert_eq!(
    utc_datetime!(2021-01-01 0:00).to_iso_week_date(),
    (2020, 53, Friday)
);
```

[Source](https://time-rs.github.io/src/time/utc_date_time.rs.html#1249-1257)

#### pub(crate) const fn [is_valid_leap_second_stand_in](https://time-rs.github.io#method.is_valid_leap_second_stand_in)(self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

**crate feature**only.

`parsing`A helper method to check if the `UtcDateTime` is a valid representation of a leap second.
Leap seconds, when parsed, are represented as the preceding nanosecond. However, leap
seconds can only occur as the last second of a month UTC.

# UtcOffset in time::utc_offset - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/utc_offset/struct.UtcOffset.html

```
pub struct UtcOffset {
    seconds: ri8<{ _ }, { _ }>,
    minutes: ri8<{ _ }, { _ }>,
    hours: ri8<-25, 25>,
}
```
## Expand description

An offset from UTC.

This struct can store values up to ±25:59:59. If you need support outside this range, please file an issue with your use case.

## Fields[§](https://time-rs.github.io#fields)

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.minutes)

`minutes: ri8<{ _ }, { _ }>`**little-endian**only.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structfield.hours)

`hours: ri8<-25, 25>`**little-endian**only.

Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset of the hours, minutes, and seconds provided, the
validity of which must be guaranteed by the caller. All three parameters must have the same
sign.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#safety)Safety

- Hours must be in the range `-25..=25`.
- Minutes must be in the range `-59..=59`.
- Seconds must be in the range `-59..=59`.

While the signs of the parameters are required to match to avoid bugs, this is not a safety invariant.

Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset by the number of hours, minutes, and seconds
provided.

The sign of all three components should match. If they do not, all smaller components will have their signs flipped.

pub enum Weekday {
    Monday = 0,
    Tuesday = 1,
    Wednesday = 2,
    Thursday = 3,
    Friday = 4,
    Saturday = 5,
    Sunday = 6,
}Expand description Days of the week.

As order is dependent on context (Sunday could be either two days after or five days before
Friday), this type does not implement `PartialOrd` or `Ord`.

# time::format_description - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/format_description/index.html

**crate features**only.

`formatting` or `parsing`## Expand description

Description of how types should be formatted and parsed.

The formatted value will be output to the provided writer. Format descriptions can be
[well-known](https://time-rs.github.io/well_known/index.html) or obtained by using the
[ format_description!](https://time-rs.github.io/macros/macro.format_description.html) macro or a function listed below.

For examples, see the implementors of [Formattable](https://time-rs.github.io/formatting/formattable/trait.Formattable.html),
e.g. [ well_known::Rfc3339](https://time-rs.github.io/well_known/rfc3339/struct.Rfc3339.html).

## Re-exports[§](https://time-rs.github.io#reexports)

- [f64_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.f64_10_pow_x.html)🔒- 10_ - pow_ - x
- Helper function to obtain 10^x, guaranteeing determinism for x ≤ 9. For these cases, the
function optimizes to a lookup table. For x ≥ 10, it falls back to `10_f64.powi(x)`. The only situation where this would occur is if the user explicitly requests such precision when configuring the ISO 8601 well known format. All other possibilities max out at nine digits.

# time::num_fmt - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/num_fmt/index.html

## Expand description

Formatting utilities for numbers.

These functions are low-level, but are designed to be *extremely* fast for their designed use
cases. They have strict requirements, and may not return the most ergonomic types to avoid
unnecessary allocations and copying.

## Structs[§](https://time-rs.github.io#structs)

- [Stack](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.StackStr.html)🔒- Str
- A string type with a maximum length known at compile time, stored on the stack.
- [Stack](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.StackTrailingStr.html)🔒- Trailing - Str
- A string type with a maximum length known at compile time, stored on the stack.

## Statics[§](https://time-rs.github.io#statics)

- [SINGLE_](https://time-rs.github.io/static.SINGLE_DIGITS.html)🔒- DIGITS
- [SPACE_](https://time-rs.github.io/static.SPACE_PADDED_PAIRS.html)🔒- PADDED_ - PAIRS - `formatting`
- [ZERO_](https://time-rs.github.io/static.ZERO_PADDED_PAIRS.html)🔒- PADDED_ - PAIRS

## Functions[§](https://time-rs.github.io#functions)

- [div_100](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.div_100.html)🔒
- [div_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.div_rem_1e16.html)🔒- rem_ - 1e16 - `formatting`
- [enc_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.enc_16lsd.html)🔒- 16lsd - ⚠- `formatting`
- Encodes the 16 least-significant decimals of n into `buf[OFFSET..OFFSET + 16]`.
- [five_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.five_digits_zero_padded.html)🔒- digits_ - zero_ - padded - `formatting`
- Obtain three strings which together represent `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading zeros are included if the number has fewer than 5 digits. The first string will be empty if`n`is less than 10,000.
- [four_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.four_digits_space_padded.html)🔒- digits_ - space_ - padded - `formatting`
- Obtain two strings of two ASCII digits each representing `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading spaces are included if the number has fewer than 4 digits.
- [four_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.four_digits_zero_padded.html)🔒- digits_ - zero_ - padded
- Obtain two strings of two ASCII digits each representing `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading zeros are included if the number has fewer than 4 digits.
- [four_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.four_to_six_digits.html)🔒- to_ - six_ - digits
- Obtain three strings which together represent `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading zeros are included if the number has fewer than 4 digits. The first string will be empty if`n`is less than 10,000.
- [mulhi](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.mulhi.html)🔒- `formatting`
- Multiply unsigned 128 bit integers, return upper 128 bits of the result
- [one_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.one_to_four_digits_no_padding.html)🔒- to_ - four_ - digits_ - no_ - padding - `formatting`
- Obtain two strings of ASCII digits representing `n`. The first string is the most significant. No leading zeros or spaces are included.
- [one_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.one_to_three_digits_no_padding.html)🔒- to_ - three_ - digits_ - no_ - padding - `formatting`
- Obtain two strings of ASCII digits representing `n`. The first string is most significant. No leading zeros or spaces are included.
- [one_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.one_to_two_digits_no_padding.html)🔒- to_ - two_ - digits_ - no_ - padding

- Obtain a string containing a single ASCII digit representing `n`.
- [six_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.six_digits_zero_padded.html)🔒- digits_ - zero_ - padded - `formatting`
- Obtain three strings which together represent `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading zeroes are included if the number has fewer than 6 digits.

- Safety
- [subsecond_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.subsecond_from_nanos.html)🔒- from_ - nanos
- Obtain five strings which together represent `n`, which is a number of nanoseconds.
- [three_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.three_digits_space_padded.html)🔒- digits_ - space_ - padded - `formatting`
- Obtain two strings of ASCII digits representing `n`. The first string is the most significant. Leading spaces are included if the number has fewer than 3 digits.

- Format a `u128`into a string with no padding.
- [write_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.write_one_digit.html)🔒- one_ - digit - ⚠

- [write_](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.write_two_digits.html)🔒- two_ - digits - ⚠

# time::quickcheck - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/internal-api/time/quickcheck/index.html

**crate feature**only.

`quickcheck`## Expand description

Implementations of the [ quickcheck::Arbitrary](quickcheck::Arbitrary) trait.

This enables users to write tests such as this, and have test values provided automatically:

[ⓘ](https://time-rs.github.io)

```
use quickcheck::quickcheck;
use time::Date;
struct DateRange {
    from: Date,
    to: Date,
}
impl DateRange {
    fn new(from: Date, to: Date) -> Result<Self, ()> {
        Ok(DateRange { from, to })
    }
}
quickcheck! {
    fn date_range_is_well_defined(from: Date, to: Date) -> bool {
        let r = DateRange::new(from, to);
        if from <= to {
            r.is_ok()
        } else {
            r.is_err()
        }
    }
}
```
An implementation for `Instant` is intentionally omitted since its values are only meaningful in
relation to a [ Duration](https://time-rs.github.io/duration/struct.Duration.html), and obtaining an

`Instant` from a [is very simple anyway.](https://time-rs.github.io/duration/struct.Duration.html)

`Duration`## Macros[§](https://time-rs.github.io#macros)

- [arbitrary_](https://time-rs.github.io/macro.arbitrary_between.html)🔒- between
- Obtain an arbitrary value between the minimum and maximum inclusive.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/src/time/lib.rs.html

# time/lib.rs

[1](https://time-rs.github.io#1)//! # Feature flags
[2](https://time-rs.github.io#2)//!
[3](https://time-rs.github.io#3)//! This crate exposes a number of features. These can be enabled or disabled as shown
[4](https://time-rs.github.io#4)//! [in Cargo's documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html). Features
[5](https://time-rs.github.io#5)//! are _disabled_ by default unless otherwise noted.
[6](https://time-rs.github.io#6)//!
[7](https://time-rs.github.io#7)//! Reliance on a given feature is always indicated alongside the item definition.
[8](https://time-rs.github.io#8)//!
[9](https://time-rs.github.io#9)//! - `std` (_enabled by default, implicitly enables `alloc`_)
[10](https://time-rs.github.io#10)//!
[11](https://time-rs.github.io#11)//!   This enables a number of features that depend on the standard library.
[12](https://time-rs.github.io#12)//!
[13](https://time-rs.github.io#13)//! - `alloc` (_enabled by default via `std`_)
[14](https://time-rs.github.io#14)//!
[15](https://time-rs.github.io#15)//!   Enables a number of features that require the ability to dynamically allocate memory.
[16](https://time-rs.github.io#16)//!
[17](https://time-rs.github.io#17)//! - `macros`
[18](https://time-rs.github.io#18)//!
[19](https://time-rs.github.io#19)//!   Enables macros that provide compile-time verification of values and intuitive syntax.
[20](https://time-rs.github.io#20)//!
[21](https://time-rs.github.io#21)//! - `formatting` (_implicitly enables `std`_)
[22](https://time-rs.github.io#22)//!
[23](https://time-rs.github.io#23)//!   Enables formatting of most structs.
[24](https://time-rs.github.io#24)//!
[25](https://time-rs.github.io#25)//! - `parsing`
[26](https://time-rs.github.io#26)//!
[27](https://time-rs.github.io#27)//!   Enables parsing of most structs.
[28](https://time-rs.github.io#28)//!
[29](https://time-rs.github.io#29)//! - `local-offset` (_implicitly enables `std`_)
[30](https://time-rs.github.io#30)//!
[31](https://time-rs.github.io#31)//!   This feature enables a number of methods that allow obtaining the system's UTC offset.
[32](https://time-rs.github.io#32)//!
[33](https://time-rs.github.io#33)//! - `large-dates`
[34](https://time-rs.github.io#34)//!
[35](https://time-rs.github.io#35)//!   By default, only years within the ±9999 range (inclusive) are supported. If you need support
[36](https://time-rs.github.io#36)//!   for years outside this range, consider enabling this feature; the supported range will be
[37](https://time-rs.github.io#37)//!   increased to ±999,999.
[38](https://time-rs.github.io#38)//!
[39](https://time-rs.github.io#39)//!   Note that enabling this feature has some costs, as it means forgoing some optimizations.
[40](https://time-rs.github.io#40)//!   Ambiguities may be introduced when parsing that would not otherwise exist.
[41](https://time-rs.github.io#41)//!
[42](https://time-rs.github.io#42)//! - `serde`
[43](https://time-rs.github.io#43)//!
[44](https://time-rs.github.io#44)//!   Enables [`serde`](https://docs.rs/serde) support for all types.
[45](https://time-rs.github.io#45)//!
[46](https://time-rs.github.io#46)//! - `serde-human-readable` (_implicitly enables `serde`, `formatting`, and `parsing`_)
[47](https://time-rs.github.io#47)//!
[48](https://time-rs.github.io#48)//!   Allows `serde` representations to use a human-readable format. This is determined by the
[49](https://time-rs.github.io#49)//!   serializer, not the user. If this feature is not enabled or if the serializer requests a
[50](https://time-rs.github.io#50)//!   non-human-readable format, a format optimized for binary representation will be used.
[51](https://time-rs.github.io#51)//!
[52](https://time-rs.github.io#52)//!   Libraries should never enable this feature, as the decision of what format to use should be up
[53](https://time-rs.github.io#53)//!   to the user.
[54](https://time-rs.github.io#54)//!
[55](https://time-rs.github.io#55)//! - `rand` (_implicitly enables `rand08`, `rand09`, and `rand010`_)
[56](https://time-rs.github.io#56)//!
[57](https://time-rs.github.io#57)//!   Previously, this would enable support for `rand` 0.8. Since the release of `rand` 0.9, the
[58](https://time-rs.github.io#58)//!   feature has been split into `rand08` and `rand09` to allow support for both versions. `rand`
[59](https://time-rs.github.io#59)//!   0.10 has since been added. For backwards compatibility and simplicity, this feature enables
[60](https://time-rs.github.io#60)//!   support for _all_ series.
[61](https://time-rs.github.io#61)//!
[62](https://time-rs.github.io#62)//!   It is strongly recommended to enable the version you need directly, as enabling `rand` will
[63](https://time-rs.github.io#63)//!   needlessly pull in all versions.
[64](https://time-rs.github.io#64)//!
[65](https://time-rs.github.io#65)//! - `rand08`, `rand09`, `rand010`
[66](https://time-rs.github.io#66)//!
[67](https://time-rs.github.io#67)//!   Enables [`rand` 0.8](https://docs.rs/rand/0.8), [`rand` 0.9](https://docs.rs/rand/0.9), and
[68](https://time-rs.github.io#68)//!   [`rand` 0.10](https://docs.rs/rand/0.10) support for all types, respectively.
[69](https://time-rs.github.io#69)//!
[70](https://time-rs.github.io#70)//! - `quickcheck` (_implicitly enables `alloc`_)
[71](https://time-rs.github.io#71)//!
[72](https://time-rs.github.io#72)//!   Enables [quickcheck](https://docs.rs/quickcheck) support for all types.
[73](https://time-rs.github.io#73)//!
[74](https://time-rs.github.io#74)//! - `wasm-bindgen`
[75](https://time-rs.github.io#75)//!
[76](https://time-rs.github.io#76)//!   Enables [`wasm-bindgen`](https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen) support for converting
[77](https://time-rs.github.io#77)//!   [JavaScript dates](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-bindgen/api/js_sys/struct.Date.html), as
[78](https://time-rs.github.io#78)//!   well as obtaining the UTC offset from JavaScript.
[79](https://time-rs.github.io#79)
[80](https://time-rs.github.io#80)#![doc(html_playground_url = "https://play.rust-lang.org")]
[81](https://time-rs.github.io#81)#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg, doc_notable_trait))]

}## Expand description

A unified error type for anything returned by a method in the time crate.

This can be used when you either don’t know or don’t care about the exact error returned.
`Result<_, time::Error>` (or its alias `time::Result<_>`) will work in these situations.

[1](#1)macro_rules! div_floor {
[5](#5)    ($self:expr, $rhs:expr) => {
[6](#6)        match ($self, $rhs) {
[7](#7)            (this, rhs) => {
[8](#8)                let d = this / rhs;
[9](#9)                let r = this % rhs;
[10](#10)
[11](#11)                let correction = (this ^ rhs) >> (size_of_val(&this) * 8 - 1);
[18](#18)                if r != 0 { d + correction } else { d }

[27](#27)    (@most_once $value:expr, $min:literal.. $max:expr) => {
[28](#28)        match ($value, $min, $max) {
[29](#29)            (value, min, max) => {
[30](#30)                if crate::hint::likely(value >= min) {
[31](#31)                    if crate::hint::likely(value < max) {
[32](#32)                        (value, 0)
[33](#33)                    } else {
[34](#34)                        (value - (max - min), 1)
[35](#35)                    }
[36](#36)                } else {
[37](#37)                    (value + (max - min), -1)
[38](#38)                }
[39](#39)            }

[42](#42)    (@most_twice $value:expr, $min:literal.. $max:expr) => {
[43](#43)        match ($value, $min, $max) {
[44](#44)            (value, min, max) => {
[45](#45)                if crate::hint::likely(value >= min) {
[46](#46)                    if crate::hint::likely(value < max) {
[47](#47)                        (value, 0)
[48](#48)                    } else if value < 2 * max - min {
[49](#49)                        (value - (max - min), 1)
[50](#50)                    } else {
[51](#51)                        (value - 2 * (max - min), 2)
[52](#52)                    }
[53](#53)                } else {
[54](#54)                    if value >= min - max {
[55](#55)                        (value + (max - min), -1)
[56](#56)                    } else {
[57](#57)                        (value + 2 * (max - min), -2)
[58](#58)                    }
[59](#59)                }
[60](#60)            }
[61](#61)        }
[62](#62)    };
[63](#63)    (@most_thrice $value:expr, $min:literal.. $max:expr) => {
[64](#64)        match ($value, $min, $max) {
[65](#65)            (value, min, max) => {
[66](#66)                if crate::hint::likely(value >= min) {
[67](#67)                    if crate::hint::likely(value < max) {
[68](#68)                        (value, 0)
[69](#69)                    } else if value < 2 * max - min {
[70](#70)                        (value - (max - min), 1)
[71](#71)                    } else if value < 3 * max - 2 * min {
[72](#72)                        (value - 2 * (max - min), 2)
[73](#73)                    } else {
[74](#74)                        (value - 3 * (max - min), 3)
[75](#75)                    }
[76](#76)                } else {
[77](#77)                    if value >= min - max {
[78](#78)                        (value + (max - min), -1)
[79](#79)                    } else if value >= 2 * (min - max) {
[80](#80)                        (value + 2 * (max - min), -2)
[81](#81)                    } else {

[95](#95)    ($from:ident in $min:literal.. $max:expr => $to:tt) => {
[97](#97)        #[allow(unused_comparisons, unused_assignments)]

[99](#99)        let max = $max;

[157](https://time-rs.github.io#157)const fn div_100(n: ru16<0, 9_999>) -> [ru8<0, 99>; 2] {
[158](https://time-rs.github.io#158)    const EXP: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = 19; // 19 is faster or equal to 12 even for 3 digits.
[159](https://time-rs.github.io#159)    const SIG: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) = (1 << [EXP](https://time-rs.github.io#158)) / 100 + 1;
[160](https://time-rs.github.io#160)
[161](https://time-rs.github.io#161)    let n = [n](https://time-rs.github.io#157).get();
[162](https://time-rs.github.io#162)
[163](https://time-rs.github.io#163)    let high = ([n](https://time-rs.github.io#161) as [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) * [SIG](https://time-rs.github.io#159)) >> [EXP](https://time-rs.github.io#158); // value / 100
[164](https://time-rs.github.io#164)    let low = [n](https://time-rs.github.io#161) as [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) - [high](https://time-rs.github.io#163) * 100;
[165](https://time-rs.github.io#165)
[166](https://time-rs.github.io#166)    // Safety: `high` is guaranteed to be less than 100 and `low` is guaranteed to be less than 100
[167](https://time-rs.github.io#167)    // due to the arithmetic above.
[168](https://time-rs.github.io#168)    unsafe {
[169](https://time-rs.github.io#169)        [
[170](https://time-rs.github.io#170)            ru8::new_unchecked([high](https://time-rs.github.io#163) as [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
[171](https://time-rs.github.io#171)            ru8::new_unchecked([low](https://time-rs.github.io#164) as [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
[172](https://time-rs.github.io#172)        ]
[173](https://time-rs.github.io#173)    }

[234](https://time-rs.github.io#234)/// Obtain two strings of ASCII digits representing `n`. The first string is the most significant.

[300](https://time-rs.github.io#300)pub(crate) const fn four_to_six_digits(n: ru32<0, 999_999>) -> [&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html); 3] {
[301](https://time-rs.github.io#301)    let n = [n](https://time-rs.github.io#300).get();
[302](https://time-rs.github.io#302)
[303](https://time-rs.github.io#303)    let (first_two, remaining) = ([n](https://time-rs.github.io#301) / 10_000, [n](https://time-rs.github.io#301) % 10_000);
[304](https://time-rs.github.io#304)
[305](https://time-rs.github.io#305)    let size = 2 - ([first_two](https://time-rs.github.io#303) < 10) as [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html) - ([first_two](https://time-rs.github.io#303) == 0) as [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);

[313](https://time-rs.github.io#313)        [four_digits_zero_padded](https://time-rs.github.io#277-280)(unsafe { ru16::new_unchecked([remaining](https://time-rs.github.io#303) as [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) });

[382](https://time-rs.github.io#382)/// Obtain a string of 1 to 9 ASCII digits representing `n`, which is a number of nanoseconds.

[404](https://time-rs.github.io#404)    // Ensure that digits 2 thru 9 are stored as a single array that is 8-aligned. This allows the

[406](https://time-rs.github.io#406)    let buf = [Digits](https://time-rs.github.io#390-394) {

[421](https://time-rs.github.io#421)    // By converting the bytes into a single integer, we can effectively perform an equality check
[422](https://time-rs.github.io#422)    // against b'0' for all bytes at once. This is actually faster than using portable SIMD (even
[423](https://time-rs.github.io#423)    // with `-Ctarget-cpu=native`).
[424](https://time-rs.github.io#424)    let bitmask = [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)::[from_le_bytes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html#method.from_le_bytes)([buf](https://time-rs.github.io#406).digits_2_thru_9) ^ [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)::[from_le_bytes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html#method.from_le_bytes)([b'0'; 8]);
[425](https://time-rs.github.io#425)    let digits_to_truncate = [bitmask](https://time-rs.github.io#424).[leading_zeros](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html#method.leading_zeros)() / 8;
[426](https://time-rs.github.io#426)    let len = 9 - [digits_to_truncate](https://time-rs.github.io#425) as [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);

[428](https://time-rs.github.io#428)    // Safety: All bytes are initialized and valid UTF-8, and `len` represents the number of bytes
[429](https://time-rs.github.io#429)    // we wish to display (that is between 1 and 9 inclusive). `Digits` is `#[repr(C)]`, so the
[430](https://time-rs.github.io#430)    // layout is guaranteed.
[431](https://time-rs.github.io#431)    unsafe {
[432](https://time-rs.github.io#432)        [StackStr](https://time-rs.github.io#35-38)::[new](https://time-rs.github.io#46-49)(
[433](https://time-rs.github.io#433)            *(&raw const [buf](https://time-rs.github.io#406))
[434](https://time-rs.github.io#434)                .[byte_add](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html#method.byte_add)([core::mem::offset_of!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/macro.offset_of.html)(Digits, digit_1))

[437](https://time-rs.github.io#437)        )

[441](https://time-rs.github.io#441)/// Format a `u64` into a string with no padding.

[443](https://time-rs.github.io#443)pub(crate) const fn u64_pad_none(value: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) -> [StackTrailingStr](https://time-rs.github.io#68-71)<20> {
[444](https://time-rs.github.io#444)    let mut bytes = [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)::[uninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html#method.uninit)(); 20];

[450](https://time-rs.github.io#450)        offset -= 4;

[452](https://time-rs.github.io#452)        remain /= 1_00_00;

[458](https://time-rs.github.io#458)            write_two_digits(&mut bytes, offset + 2, pair2);
[459](https://time-rs.github.io#459)        }
[460](https://time-rs.github.io#460)    }
[461](https://time-rs.github.io#461)
[462](https://time-rs.github.io#462)    if [remain](https://time-rs.github.io#447) > 9 {
[463](https://time-rs.github.io#463)        [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#446) -= 2;
[464](https://time-rs.github.io#464)
[465](https://time-rs.github.io#465)        // Safety: `remain` is guaranteed to be less than 10,000 due to the loop above.
[466](https://time-rs.github.io#466)        let [last, pair] = [div_100](https://time-rs.github.io#157-174)(unsafe { ru16::new_unchecked([remain](https://time-rs.github.io#447) as [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) });

[468](https://time-rs.github.io#468)        // Safety: `buf` is at least `offset + 2` bytes long.
[469](https://time-rs.github.io#469)        unsafe { [write_two_digits](https://time-rs.github.io#116-125)(&mut [bytes](https://time-rs.github.io#444), [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#446), [pair](https://time-rs.github.io#466)) };
[470](https://time-rs.github.io#470)    }
[471](https://time-rs.github.io#471)
[472](https://time-rs.github.io#472)    if [remain](https://time-rs.github.io#447) != 0 || [value](https://time-rs.github.io#443) == 0 {
[473](https://time-rs.github.io#473)        [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#446) -= 1;
[474](https://time-rs.github.io#474)
[475](https://time-rs.github.io#475)        let last = [remain](https://time-rs.github.io#447) as [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html) & 15;
[476](https://time-rs.github.io#476)        // Safety: `offset` is known to be in bounds, and the value is known to be less than 10 due
[477](https://time-rs.github.io#477)        // to the conditionals and bitwise AND above.
[478](https://time-rs.github.io#478)        unsafe { [write_one_digit](https://time-rs.github.io#133-142)(&mut [bytes](https://time-rs.github.io#444), [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#446), ru8::new_unchecked([last](https://time-rs.github.io#475))) };
[479](https://time-rs.github.io#479)    }

[482](https://time-rs.github.io#482)    unsafe { [StackTrailingStr](https://time-rs.github.io#68-71)::[new](https://time-rs.github.io#78-81)([bytes](https://time-rs.github.io#444), [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#446)) }

[494](https://time-rs.github.io#494)        ([mod_1e16](https://time-rs.github.io#492).get(), 39)

[502](https://time-rs.github.io#502)        if [quot2](https://time-rs.github.io#501) == 0 {
[503](https://time-rs.github.io#503)            ([mod2](https://time-rs.github.io#501).get(), 23)
[504](https://time-rs.github.io#504)        } else {
[505](https://time-rs.github.io#505)            // Write digits at buf[7..23].
[506](https://time-rs.github.io#506)            // Safety: `bytes` is 39 bytes long, so writing at offset 7 for 16 bytes is sound.

[508](https://time-rs.github.io#508)            // Safety: `quot2`` has at most 7 decimals remaining after two 1e16 divisions.
[509](https://time-rs.github.io#509)            ([quot2](https://time-rs.github.io#501) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html), 7)

[511](https://time-rs.github.io#511)    };

[514](https://time-rs.github.io#514)    while remain > 999 {
[515](https://time-rs.github.io#515)        offset -= 4;
[516](https://time-rs.github.io#516)
[517](https://time-rs.github.io#517)        // pull two pairs
[518](https://time-rs.github.io#518)        let quad = remain % 1_00_00;
[519](https://time-rs.github.io#519)        remain /= 1_00_00;
[520](https://time-rs.github.io#520)        // Safety: `quad` is guaranteed to be less than 10,000 due to the modulus above.

[522](https://time-rs.github.io#522)        // Safety: `buf` is at least `offset + 4` bytes long.
[523](https://time-rs.github.io#523)        unsafe {
[524](https://time-rs.github.io#524)            write_two_digits(&mut bytes, offset, pair1);
[525](https://time-rs.github.io#525)            write_two_digits(&mut bytes, offset + 2, pair2);
[526](https://time-rs.github.io#526)        }
[527](https://time-rs.github.io#527)    }
[528](https://time-rs.github.io#528)
[529](https://time-rs.github.io#529)    // Format per two digits from the lookup table.
[530](https://time-rs.github.io#530)    if [remain](https://time-rs.github.io#493) > 9 {
[531](https://time-rs.github.io#531)        [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#493) -= 2;
[532](https://time-rs.github.io#532)
[533](https://time-rs.github.io#533)        // Safety: `remain` is guaranteed to be less than 10,000 due to the loop above.
[534](https://time-rs.github.io#534)        let [last, pair] = [div_100](https://time-rs.github.io#157-174)(unsafe { ru16::new_unchecked([remain](https://time-rs.github.io#493) as [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) });
[535](https://time-rs.github.io#535)        [remain](https://time-rs.github.io#493) = [last](https://time-rs.github.io#534).get() as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[536](https://time-rs.github.io#536)        // Safety: `buf` is at least `offset + 2` bytes long.
[537](https://time-rs.github.io#537)        unsafe { [write_two_digits](https://time-rs.github.io#116-125)(&mut [bytes](https://time-rs.github.io#489), [offset](https://time-rs.github.io#493), [pair](https://time-rs.github.io#534)) };

[555](https://time-rs.github.io#555)/// Encodes the 16 least-significant decimals of n into `buf[OFFSET..OFFSET + 16]`.
[556](https://time-rs.github.io#556)///
[557](https://time-rs.github.io#557)/// # Safety
[558](https://time-rs.github.io#558)///
[559](https://time-rs.github.io#559)/// - `buf` must be at least `OFFSET + 16` bytes long.
[560](https://time-rs.github.io#560)#[cfg(feature = "formatting")]
[561](https://time-rs.github.io#561)const unsafe fn enc_16lsd<const OFFSET: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
[562](https://time-rs.github.io#562)    buf: &mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>],
[563](https://time-rs.github.io#563)    n: ru64<0, 9999_9999_9999_9999>,
[564](https://time-rs.github.io#564)) {
[565](https://time-rs.github.io#565)    // Consume the least-significant decimals from a working copy.
[566](https://time-rs.github.io#566)    let mut remain = [n](https://time-rs.github.io#563).get();
[567](https://time-rs.github.io#567)
[568](https://time-rs.github.io#568)    let mut quad_index = 3;
[569](https://time-rs.github.io#569)    while quad_index >= 1 {
[570](https://time-rs.github.io#570)        let quad = remain % 1_00_00;
[571](https://time-rs.github.io#571)        remain /= 1_00_00;
[572](https://time-rs.github.io#572)        // Safety: `quad` is guaranteed to be less than 10,000 due to the modulus above.
[573](https://time-rs.github.io#573)        let [pair1, pair2] = div_100(unsafe { ru16::new_unchecked(quad as u16) });
[574](https://time-rs.github.io#574)        // Safety: `buf` is at least `quad_index * 4 + OFFSET + 4` bytes long.
[575](https://time-rs.github.io#575)        unsafe {
[576](https://time-rs.github.io#576)            write_two_digits(buf, quad_index * 4 + OFFSET, pair1);
[577](https://time-rs.github.io#577)            write_two_digits(buf, quad_index * 4 + OFFSET + 2, pair2);
[578](https://time-rs.github.io#578)        }
[579](https://time-rs.github.io#579)        quad_index -= 1;
[580](https://time-rs.github.io#580)    }
[581](https://time-rs.github.io#581)
[582](https://time-rs.github.io#582)    // Safety: `remain` is guaranteed to be less than 10,000 due the range of `n` and the arithmetic
[583](https://time-rs.github.io#583)    // in the loop above.
[584](https://time-rs.github.io#584)    let [pair1, pair2] = [div_100](https://time-rs.github.io#157-174)(unsafe { ru16::new_unchecked([remain](https://time-rs.github.io#566) as [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)) });
[585](https://time-rs.github.io#585)    // Safety: `buf` is at least `OFFSET + 4` bytes long.
[586](https://time-rs.github.io#586)    unsafe {
[587](https://time-rs.github.io#587)        [write_two_digits](https://time-rs.github.io#116-125)([buf](https://time-rs.github.io#562), [OFFSET](https://time-rs.github.io#561), [pair1](https://time-rs.github.io#584));
[588](https://time-rs.github.io#588)        [write_two_digits](https://time-rs.github.io#116-125)([buf](https://time-rs.github.io#562), [OFFSET](https://time-rs.github.io#561) + 2, [pair2](https://time-rs.github.io#584));
[589](https://time-rs.github.io#589)    }
[590](https://time-rs.github.io#590)}
[591](https://time-rs.github.io#591)
[592](https://time-rs.github.io#592)// Euclidean division plus remainder with constant 1e16 basically consumes 16
[593](https://time-rs.github.io#593)// decimals from n.
[594](https://time-rs.github.io#594)#[cfg(feature = "formatting")]
[595](https://time-rs.github.io#595)const fn div_rem_1e16(n: [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html)) -> ([u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html), ru64<0, 9999_9999_9999_9999>) {
[596](https://time-rs.github.io#596)    const D: [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) = 1_0000_0000_0000_0000;
[597](https://time-rs.github.io#597)    if [n](https://time-rs.github.io#595) < [D](https://time-rs.github.io#596) {
[598](https://time-rs.github.io#598)        // Safety: We just checked that `n` is in range.
[599](https://time-rs.github.io#599)        return (0, unsafe { ru64::new_unchecked([n](https://time-rs.github.io#595) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) });
[600](https://time-rs.github.io#600)    }
[601](https://time-rs.github.io#601)
[602](https://time-rs.github.io#602)    const M_HIGH: [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) = 76_624_777_043_294_442_917_917_351_357_515_459_181;
[603](https://time-rs.github.io#603)    const SH_POST: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html) = 51;
[604](https://time-rs.github.io#604)
[605](https://time-rs.github.io#605)    // n.widening_mul(M_HIGH).1 >> SH_POST
[606](https://time-rs.github.io#606)    let quot = [mulhi](https://time-rs.github.io#615-630)([n](https://time-rs.github.io#595), [M_HIGH](https://time-rs.github.io#602)) >> [SH_POST](https://time-rs.github.io#603);
[607](https://time-rs.github.io#607)    let rem = [n](https://time-rs.github.io#595) - [quot](https://time-rs.github.io#606) * [D](https://time-rs.github.io#596);
[608](https://time-rs.github.io#608)    // Safety: The arithmetic above ensures that `rem` is in range.
[609](https://time-rs.github.io#609)    ([quot](https://time-rs.github.io#606), unsafe { ru64::new_unchecked([rem](https://time-rs.github.io#607) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) })
[610](https://time-rs.github.io#610)}
[611](https://time-rs.github.io#611)
[612](https://time-rs.github.io#612)/// Multiply unsigned 128 bit integers, return upper 128 bits of the result
[613](https://time-rs.github.io#613)#[inline]
[614](https://time-rs.github.io#614)#[cfg(feature = "formatting")]
[615](https://time-rs.github.io#615)const fn mulhi(x: [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html), y: [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html)) -> [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) {
[616](https://time-rs.github.io#616)    let x_lo = [x](https://time-rs.github.io#615) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[617](https://time-rs.github.io#617)    let x_hi = ([x](https://time-rs.github.io#615) >> 64) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[618](https://time-rs.github.io#618)    let y_lo = [y](https://time-rs.github.io#615) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[619](https://time-rs.github.io#619)    let y_hi = ([y](https://time-rs.github.io#615) >> 64) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[620](https://time-rs.github.io#620)
[621](https://time-rs.github.io#621)    // handle possibility of overflow
[622](https://time-rs.github.io#622)    let carry = ([x_lo](https://time-rs.github.io#616) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) * [y_lo](https://time-rs.github.io#618) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html)) >> 64;
[623](https://time-rs.github.io#623)    let m = [x_lo](https://time-rs.github.io#616) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) * [y_hi](https://time-rs.github.io#619) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) + [carry](https://time-rs.github.io#622);
[624](https://time-rs.github.io#624)    let high1 = [m](https://time-rs.github.io#623) >> 64;
[625](https://time-rs.github.io#625)
[626](https://time-rs.github.io#626)    let m_lo = [m](https://time-rs.github.io#623) as [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html);
[627](https://time-rs.github.io#627)    let high2 = ([x_hi](https://time-rs.github.io#617) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) * [y_lo](https://time-rs.github.io#618) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) + [m_lo](https://time-rs.github.io#626) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html)) >> 64;
[628](https://time-rs.github.io#628)
[629](https://time-rs.github.io#629)    [x_hi](https://time-rs.github.io#617) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) * [y_hi](https://time-rs.github.io#619) as [u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) + [high1](https://time-rs.github.io#624) + [high2](https://time-rs.github.io#627)
[630](https://time-rs.github.io#630)}

# days_in_year in time::util - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/util/fn.days_in_year.html

# Function days_in_year

[Source](../../src/time_core/util.rs.html#103) `pub const fn days_in_year(year: `[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)

## Expand description

Get the number of calendar days in a given year.

The returned value will always be either 365 or 366.

```
assert_eq!(days_in_year(1900), 365);
assert_eq!(days_in_year(2000), 366);
assert_eq!(days_in_year(2004), 366);
assert_eq!(days_in_year(2005), 365);
assert_eq!(days_in_year(2100), 365);
```

[183](https://time-rs.github.io#183)    /// Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset by the number of hours, minutes, and seconds
[184](https://time-rs.github.io#184)    /// provided.

[192](https://time-rs.github.io#192)    /// assert_eq!(UtcOffset::from_hms(1, -2, -3)?.as_hms(), (1, 2, 3));
[193](https://time-rs.github.io#193)    /// # Ok::<_, time::Error>(())
[194](https://time-rs.github.io#194)    /// ```

[199](https://time-rs.github.io#199)        seconds: [i8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i8.html),

[208](https://time-rs.github.io#208)    /// Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset of the hours, minutes, and seconds provided. All
[209](https://time-rs.github.io#209)    /// three parameters must have the same sign.
[210](https://time-rs.github.io#210)    ///
[211](https://time-rs.github.io#211)    /// While the signs of the parameters are required to match, this is not a safety invariant.
[212](https://time-rs.github.io#212)    #[inline]
[213](https://time-rs.github.io#213)    #[track_caller]
[214](https://time-rs.github.io#214)    pub(crate) const fn from_hms_ranged_unchecked(
[215](https://time-rs.github.io#215)        hours: [Hours](https://time-rs.github.io#32),
[216](https://time-rs.github.io#216)        minutes: [Minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#34-35),
[217](https://time-rs.github.io#217)        seconds: [Seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#37-38),
[218](https://time-rs.github.io#218)    ) -> Self {
[219](https://time-rs.github.io#219)        if [hours](https://time-rs.github.io#215).get() < 0 {
[220](https://time-rs.github.io#220)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(minutes.get() <= 0);
[221](https://time-rs.github.io#221)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(seconds.get() <= 0);
[222](https://time-rs.github.io#222)        } else if [hours](https://time-rs.github.io#215).get() > 0 {
[223](https://time-rs.github.io#223)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(minutes.get() >= 0);
[224](https://time-rs.github.io#224)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(seconds.get() >= 0);
[225](https://time-rs.github.io#225)        }
[226](https://time-rs.github.io#226)        if [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#216).get() < 0 {
[227](https://time-rs.github.io#227)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(seconds.get() <= 0);
[228](https://time-rs.github.io#228)        } else if [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#216).get() > 0 {
[229](https://time-rs.github.io#229)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(seconds.get() >= 0);
[230](https://time-rs.github.io#230)        }
[231](https://time-rs.github.io#231)

[233](https://time-rs.github.io#233)            [hours](https://time-rs.github.io#215),
[234](https://time-rs.github.io#234)            [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#216),
[235](https://time-rs.github.io#235)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#217),
[236](https://time-rs.github.io#236)        }

[239](https://time-rs.github.io#239)    /// Create a `UtcOffset` representing an offset by the number of hours, minutes, and seconds
[240](https://time-rs.github.io#240)    /// provided.
[241](https://time-rs.github.io#241)    ///
[242](https://time-rs.github.io#242)    /// The sign of all three components should match. If they do not, all smaller components will
[243](https://time-rs.github.io#243)    /// have their signs flipped.
[244](https://time-rs.github.io#244)    #[inline]
[245](https://time-rs.github.io#245)    pub(crate) const fn from_hms_ranged(
[246](https://time-rs.github.io#246)        hours: [Hours](https://time-rs.github.io#32),
[247](https://time-rs.github.io#247)        mut minutes: [Minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#34-35),
[248](https://time-rs.github.io#248)        mut seconds: [Seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#37-38),
[249](https://time-rs.github.io#249)    ) -> Self {
[250](https://time-rs.github.io#250)        if ([hours](https://time-rs.github.io#246).get() > 0 && [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247).get() < 0) || ([hours](https://time-rs.github.io#246).get() < 0 && [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247).get() > 0) {
[251](https://time-rs.github.io#251)            [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247) = [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247).neg();
[252](https://time-rs.github.io#252)        }
[253](https://time-rs.github.io#253)        if ([hours](https://time-rs.github.io#246).get() > 0 && [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248).get() < 0)
[254](https://time-rs.github.io#254)            || ([hours](https://time-rs.github.io#246).get() < 0 && [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248).get() > 0)
[255](https://time-rs.github.io#255)            || ([minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247).get() > 0 && [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248).get() < 0)
[256](https://time-rs.github.io#256)            || ([minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247).get() < 0 && [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248).get() > 0)
[257](https://time-rs.github.io#257)        {
[258](https://time-rs.github.io#258)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248) = [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248).neg();
[259](https://time-rs.github.io#259)        }
[260](https://time-rs.github.io#260)
[261](https://time-rs.github.io#261)        Self {
[262](https://time-rs.github.io#262)            [hours](https://time-rs.github.io#246),
[263](https://time-rs.github.io#263)            [minutes](https://time-rs.github.io#247),
[264](https://time-rs.github.io#264)            [seconds](https://time-rs.github.io#248),
[265](https://time-rs.github.io#265)        }
[266](https://time-rs.github.io#266)    }

A unit of time representing exactly `N` nanoseconds.

#### pub const fn [per](https://time-rs.github.io#method.per)<T>(_larger: T) -> <T as DefaultOutput<[Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Nanosecond.html)>>::Output

Obtain the number of times `Nanosecond` can fit into `T`.
If `T` is smaller than `Nanosecond`, the code will fail to
compile. The return type is the smallest unsigned integer type that can represent
the value.

Valid calls:

- `Nanosecond::per(Nanosecond)`(returns- `u8`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Microsecond)`(returns- `u16`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Millisecond)`(returns- `u32`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Second)`(returns- `u32`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Minute)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Hour)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Day)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Week)`(returns- `u64`)

Obtain the number of times `Nanosecond` can fit into `T`.
If `T` is smaller than `Nanosecond`, the code will fail to
compile. The return type is any primitive numeric type that can represent the value.

Valid calls:

# Nanosecond in time_core::unit - Rust

`pub struct Nanosecond<const N: `[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html) = 1>;## Expand description

A unit of time representing exactly `N` nanoseconds.

### impl [Nanosecond](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Nanosecond.html)<1>

Obtain the number of times `Nanosecond` can fit into `T`.
If `T` is smaller than `Nanosecond`, the code will fail to
compile. The return type is the smallest unsigned integer type that can represent
the value.

Valid calls:

- `Nanosecond::per(Nanosecond)`(returns- `u8`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Microsecond)`(returns- `u16`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Millisecond)`(returns- `u32`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Second)`(returns- `u32`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Minute)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Hour)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Day)`(returns- `u64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Week)`(returns- `u64`)

Obtain the number of times `Nanosecond` can fit into `T`.
If `T` is smaller than `Nanosecond`, the code will fail to
compile. The return type is any primitive numeric type that can represent the value.

Valid calls:

- `Nanosecond::per(Nanosecond)`(returns- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `usize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `isize`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Microsecond)`(returns- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `usize`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `isize`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Millisecond)`(returns- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `usize`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `isize`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Second)`(returns- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `usize`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `isize`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Minute)`(returns- `u64`,- `u128`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Hour)`(returns- `u64`,- `u128`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Day)`(returns- `u64`,- `u128`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)
- `Nanosecond::per(Week)`(returns- `u64`,- `u128`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `f32`, or- `f64`)

`pub struct FormatDescriptionV3<'a> { /* private fields */ }`**crate features**only.

`formatting` or `parsing`## Expand description

A complete description of how to format and parse a type.

Both for forwards compatibility and to enable optimizations, this type is deliberately opaque
and cannot be constructed by users of the crate. Instead, it is returned by the
`format_description!` macro (when `version=3` is used) as well as the `parse_borrowed` and
`parse_owned` methods.

# Rfc2822 in time::format_description::well_known - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/format_description/well_known/struct.Rfc2822.html

# Struct Rfc2822

[Source](../../../src/time/format_description/well_known/rfc2822.rs.html#30) `pub struct Rfc2822;`

Available on **crate features **`formatting` or `parsing` only.

## Expand description

The format described in [RFC 2822](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2822#section-3.3).

Example: Fri, 21 Nov 1997 09:55:06 -0600

[§](#examples)Examples

```
use time_macros::datetime;
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::parse("Sat, 12 Jun 1993 13:25:19 GMT", &Rfc2822)?,
    datetime!(1993-06-12 13:25:19 +00:00)
);
```

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(1997-11-21 09:55:06 -06:00).format(&Rfc2822)?,
    "Fri, 21 Nov 1997 09:55:06 -0600"
);
```

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)

Formats the value using the given formatter.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html#tymethod.fmt)[Source](../../../src/time/parsing/parsable.rs.html#34)[§](#impl-Parsable-for-Rfc2822)Available on **crate feature **`parsing` only.

Tests for `self` and `other` values to be equal, and is used by `==`.

Tests for `!=`. The default implementation is almost always sufficient,
and should not be overridden without very good reason.

Immutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.Borrow.html#tymethod.borrow)

Mutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.BorrowMut.html#tymethod.borrow_mut)

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`clone_to_uninit`)

Performs copy-assignment from

`self` to

`dest`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.CloneToUninit.html#tymethod.clone_to_uninit)

Returns the argument unchanged.

Calls `U::from(self)`.

That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of

# Struct Rfc3339

[Source](../../../src/time/format_description/well_known/rfc3339.rs.html#30) `pub struct Rfc3339;`

Available on **crate features **`formatting` or `parsing` only.

## Expand description

The format described in [RFC 3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339#section-5.6).

Format example: 1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z

[§](#examples)Examples

```
assert_eq!(
    OffsetDateTime::parse("1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z", &Rfc3339)?,
    datetime!(1985-04-12 23:20:50.52 +00:00)
);
```

```
assert_eq!(
    datetime!(1985-04-12 23:20:50.52 +00:00).format(&Rfc3339)?,
    "1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z"
);
```

# Iso8601 in time::format_description::well_known - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/format_description/well_known/struct.Iso8601.html

`pub struct Iso8601<const CONFIG: `[EncodedConfig](https://time-rs.github.io/iso8601/type.EncodedConfig.html) = { Config::DEFAULT.encode() }>;**crate features**only.

`formatting` or `parsing`## Expand description

The format described in [ISO 8601](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html).

This implementation is of ISO 8601-1:2019. It may not be compatible with other versions.

The const parameter `CONFIG` **must** be a value that was returned by [ Config::encode](https://time-rs.github.io/iso8601/struct.Config.html#method.encode).
Passing any other value is

**unspecified behavior**.

Example: 1997-11-21T09:55:06.000000000-06:00

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#examples)Examples

## Implementations[§](https://time-rs.github.io#implementations)

An [ Iso8601](https://time-rs.github.io/struct.Iso8601.html) with the default configuration.

The following is the default behavior:

- The configuration can be used for both formatting and parsing.
- The date, time, and UTC offset are all formatted.
- Separators (such as `-`and`:`) are included.
- The year contains four digits, such that the year must be between 0 and 9999.
- The date uses the calendar format.
- The time has precision to the second and nine decimal digits.
- The UTC offset has precision to the minute.

If you need different behavior, use another associated constant. For full customization, use
[ Config::DEFAULT](https://time-rs.github.io/iso8601/struct.Config.html#associatedconstant.DEFAULT) and

[’s methods to create a custom configuration.](https://time-rs.github.io/iso8601/struct.Config.html)

`alloc` and (crate features `formatting` or `parsing`)## Expand description

Parse a sequence of items from the format description.

The syntax for the format description can be found in [the
book](https://time-rs.github.io/book/api/format-description.html). The version of the format
description is provided as the const parameter. **It is recommended to use version 3.**

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#return-type)Return type

The return type of this function depends on the version provided.

- For versions 1 and 2, the function returns `Result<Vec<BorrowedFormatItem<'_>>, InvalidFormatDescription>`.
- For version 3, the function returns `Result<FormatDescriptionV3<'_>, InvalidFormatDescription>`.

    Version<VERSION>: VersionedParser,**crate feature**only.

`alloc` and (crate features `formatting` or `parsing`)## Expand description

Parse a sequence of items from the format description.

The syntax for the format description can be found in [the
book](https://time-rs.github.io/book/api/format-description.html). The version of the format
description is provided as the const parameter.

Unlike [ parse](https://time-rs.github.io/fn.parse.html), this function returns

[, which owns its contents. This means that there is no lifetime that needs to be handled.](https://time-rs.github.io/enum.OwnedFormatItem.html)

`OwnedFormatItem`**It is recommended to use version 3.**

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#return-type)Return type

The return type of this function depends on the version provided.

- For versions 1 and 2, the function returns `Result<OwnedFormatItem, InvalidFormatDescription>`.
- For version 3, the function returns `Result<FormatDescriptionV3<'static>, InvalidFormatDescription>`.

# format_description in time::serde - Rust

Source: https://time-rs.github.io/api/time/serde/macro.format_description.html

`format_description!() { /* proc-macro */ }`**crate feature**only.

`macros` and crate feature `serde` and (crate features `formatting` or `parsing`)## Expand description

Generate a custom serializer and deserializer from a format string or an existing format.

The format description syntax accepted by this macro is the same as
[ format_description::parse()](https://time-rs.github.io/format_description/fn.parse.html), which can be found in

[the book](https://time-rs.github.io/book/api/format-description.html).

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#syntax)Syntax

**It is recommended to use version 3.** For backwards compatibility, this macro defaults to
version 1. To use version 2 or version 3, you can specify the version as the first
argument: `serde::format_description!(version = 2, mod_name, Date, FORMAT)`.

For versions 1 and 2, this macro is invoked as `serde::format_description!(mod_name, Date, FORMAT)` where `FORMAT` is either a `"<format string>"` or something that implements
[ Formattable](https://time-rs.github.io/formatting/trait.Formattable.html) and

[. This puts a module named](https://time-rs.github.io/parsing/trait.Parsable.html)

`Parsable``mod_name` in the current scope that can be used to format `Date`
structs. A submodule (`mod_name::option`) is also generated for `Option<Date>`. Both
modules are only visible in the current scope by default. To increase visibility, you can
specify `pub`, `pub(crate)`, or similar before the module name:
`serde::format_description!(pub mod_name, Date, FORMAT)`.For version 3, this macro is invoked as `serde::format_description!(mod mod_name [Date] = FORMAT)`. As with versions 1 and 2, visibility can be specified before the `mod` keyword.
The type being formatted and/or parsed must be in scope, as the macro will not import it
for you. Note: the `mod` keyword indicates that this is version 3 of the macro; specifying
`version = 3` is accepted but unnecessary.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#semantics)Semantics

The returned `Option` will contain a deserialized value if present and `None` if the field
is present but the value is `null` (or the equivalent in other formats). To return `None`
when the field is not present, you should use `#[serde(default)]` on the field.

Note: Due to [serde-rs/serde#2878](https://github.com/serde-rs/serde#2878), you will need to
apply `#[serde(default)]` if you want a missing field to deserialize as `None`.

[§](https://time-rs.github.io#examples)Examples

Using a format string:

```
use ::serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
use time::serde;
// Makes a module `mod my_format { ... }`.
serde::format_description!(my_format, OffsetDateTime, "hour=[hour], minute=[minute]");
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct SerializesWithCustom {
    #[serde(with = "my_format")]
    dt: OffsetDateTime,
    #[serde(with = "my_format::option", default)]
    maybe_dt: Option<OffsetDateTime>,
}
```
Define the format separately to be used in multiple places:

```
use ::serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
use time::serde;
use time::format_description::StaticFormatDescription;
const DATE_TIME_FORMAT: StaticFormatDescription = time::macros::format_description!(
    "hour=[hour], minute=[minute]"
);
// Makes a module `mod my_format { ... }`.
serde::format_description!(my_format, OffsetDateTime, DATE_TIME_FORMAT);
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct SerializesWithCustom {
    #[serde(with = "my_format")]
    dt: OffsetDateTime,
    #[serde(with = "my_format::option", default)]
    maybe_dt: Option<OffsetDateTime>,
}
fn main() {
    let str_ts = OffsetDateTime::now_utc().format(DATE_TIME_FORMAT).unwrap();
}
```
Customize the configuration of ISO 8601 formatting/parsing:

```
use ::serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
use time::serde;
use time::format_description::well_known::{iso8601, Iso8601};
const CONFIG: iso8601::EncodedConfig = iso8601::Config::DEFAULT
    .set_year_is_six_digits(false)
    .encode();
const FORMAT: Iso8601<CONFIG> = Iso8601::<CONFIG>;
// Makes a module `mod my_format { ... }`.
serde::format_description!(my_format, OffsetDateTime, FORMAT);
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct SerializesWithCustom {
    #[serde(with = "my_format")]
    dt: OffsetDateTime,
    #[serde(with = "my_format::option", default)]
    maybe_dt: Option<OffsetDateTime>,
}
```

[113](#113)        assert_eq!(ts, Timestamp::from_milliseconds(5_001)?);
[114](#114)
[115](#115)        let ts = Timestamp::from(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH - 5.seconds() - 1.milliseconds());
[116](#116)        assert_eq!(ts, Timestamp::from_milliseconds(-5_001)?);
[117](#117)
[118](#118)        Ok(())
[119](#119)    }
